stories.title: HC fines UP govt ₹50,000:Court asks why bail was delayed by 10 days; SHO says he was busy with Kanwar Yatra duty
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Wednesday imposed a fine of ₹50,000 on the Uttar Pradesh government for police negligence. The court, around 3 PM, said that if the police had done their work on time, the bail decision would have been made on 3rd July itself. Due to police negligence, the case remained pending for more than 10 days. In this matter, the High Court had summoned the Station In-charge, Inspector and Circle Officer, i.e., CO. During the hearing, the Station In-charge was asked why there was a 10-day delay in the bail petition. To this, the SHO said that I was busy with the Kanwar Yatra. The other two officers also gave different answers. The court expressed strong displeasure at this. The court ordered that the fine amount will be given to the petitioners. Later, if the government wishes, it can recover this from the concerned police officers after investigation. The case was related to the bail of the mother-in-law and father-in-law accused in a dowry death case. Both were granted bail. Now read the complete matter Dowry death case was registered in Bijnor A dowry death case was registered in the Chandpur police station area of Bijnor. In this case, the mother-in-law and father-in-law were made accused. Both had filed a petition in the Allahabad High Court for bail, on which the single bench of Justice Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal heard on Wednesday. After examining the record, the court said that no concrete evidence was found which could prove that the woman was tortured for dowry. The statements of witnesses also point towards a normal domestic dispute between husband and wife. Therefore, both the accused were granted bail. Expressed displeasure over the functioning of police officers The High Court expressed serious displeasure over the functioning of police officers in the case. The court said that the Joint Director (Prosecution) office had provided a copy of the bail petition to the police advocate on June 17. After this, an alert was sent to the Superintendent of Police on June 19, and a reminder was also issued on June 29. Despite this, the police did not provide the necessary instructions and case diary to the court, which affected the hearing. Case diary not sent even after court's directive The court said that on July 3, directions were given to provide the PDF of the case diary from the CCTNS portal, but the police only sent the criminal history of the accused. The required case diary was not provided. In view of the situation, the concerned station in-charge, sub-inspector and circle officer had to appear personally in the court. Officers cited leave and Kanwar duty as reasons During the hearing, the Station In-charge cited leave and Kanwar Yatra duty as reasons for the delay. Meanwhile, the Inspector termed it a 'communication gap'. The Circle Officer said that the Head Constable deployed with him had not informed him about the messages received from the High Court. The court expressed surprise at the attitude of officers passing the buck to each other and considered it a serious administrative negligence. Decision could have been made on 3rd July itself The High Court said that if the police had provided the necessary instructions and case diary on time, the bail petition could have been disposed of on 3rd July itself. Due to the negligence of the officers, the matter remained pending for more than 10 days. On this basis, the court imposed a fine of ₹50K on the Uttar Pradesh government. It directed that this amount be paid to the petitioners. Along with this, the Superintendent of Police of Bijnor was directed to investigate the concerned officials, take necessary action, and, if needed, recover this amount from them. The court has also ordered that a copy of its order be sent to the Director General of Police (DGP) of Uttar Pradesh and the Superintendent of Police of Bijnor.

stories.title: Student gangraped in moving car:Victim alleges, "They made me drink, drove me around"; 3 men abandoned her at station
stories.summary: A 19-year-old student was allegedly gang-raped inside a moving car in Lalitpur district. According to her complaint, a youth from her village called her out on Tuesday evening around 6 pm on the pretext of talking to her. He then took her away in a car, where two of his associates were already present. The three men allegedly drove her around for nearly five hours on different routes. The woman told police they forcibly made her drink alcohol before two of the accused allegedly gang-raped her. At around 11 pm, the three men abandoned her at a railway station and fled. The student somehow contacted her family and informed them about the incident. Based on her complaint, police have registered an FIR against three accused, including two who have been identified by name, and formed three teams to arrest them. The case falls under the Sadar Kotwali police station area. First read the student's ordeal... Taken 25 km away and forcibly made to drink alcohol Victim told the police that on Tuesday evening around 6 pm, she was sitting at a shop outside her house. Just then, Badal Raja from the same village arrived there. He said he needed to talk about something important. When the student asked what it was about, the accused asked her to sit in the car, and he would tell her comfortably. Being acquainted with him, she went along with him. Badal Raja took the car from the highway via Birdha towards Jakhalon town, ahead to Bandargua and Pump Canal route. During this time, Badal Raja and his companion Surendra Sen forcibly made her drink alcohol and raped her. Meanwhile, the third youth kept driving the car continuously. Drove around in the car for 5 hrs, then dropped at railway station According to the victim, the three accused took her from home around 6 PM. They kept driving her around on different routes for about five hours. After 11 PM, they abandoned her near Lalitpur Railway Station, 15 km away from her home, and fled. Somehow, she called her sister from her mobile phone and narrated the entire incident. After that, around 12 midnight, her parents reached the railway station. They took her along with them to the police station. Mother said- Daughter was not found when she returned home The victim's mother said that when she returned home from Lalitpur on Tuesday evening, her daughter was not at home. Neighbors told her that Badal Raja, a resident of the village, had taken her with him in his car. After 11 PM, the daughter called her sister's mobile, and then they came to know about the incident. Accused lives 300 m away from the student's house According to the police, the main accused, Badal Raja, is a resident of the victim's village itself. His house is about 300 meters away from the student's house. The second named accused, Surendra Sen, is a resident of a nearby village, who lives five kilometers away. Both are friends with each other. The third accused has not been identified yet. Police have not yet found any CCTV footage related to the incident. Due to the rural area and the routes through which the car was taken not having CCTV cameras installed, there are difficulties in gathering technical evidence during the investigation. CO City Ajay Kumar stated that considering the seriousness of the case, a case has been registered against two named and one unknown accused. Three police teams have been formed for the arrest of the accused. Continuous raids are being conducted at possible locations. All the accused will be arrested soon.

stories.title: GST Deputy Commissioner caught taking bribe in Varanasi:Scuffles with 4 sub-inspectors while trying to flee; vigilance team drags her into jeep
stories.summary: GST Deputy Commissioner Ambika Singh was caught red-handed taking a bribe in Varanasi. As soon as the vigilance team caught Ambika Singh, she started running away. In an attempt to escape, she even scuffled with 4 female constables. During this time, a crowd of people gathered around. The female officer kept pleading with the crowd and passersby to save her. After this, the vigilance team dragged Ambika Singh into the jeep and took her to the police station. Actually, Deputy Commissioner Ambika Singh had demanded a bribe of 50 thousand rupees from a businessman for filing returns and disposing of GST files. She had reached a restaurant near the GST Commissioner's office to take the bribe amount. She was caught during this time. The incident is from the Bhelupur police station area at 6:30 PM on Wednesday. First see 2 pictures... Now read the complete case Ajay Kumar Maurya, a resident of Bajardeeha, is a director of 'Black Smith Industries Private Limited' company. Ajay had filed his February 2023 return and GST (State) on time. However, after finding discrepancies in it, the GST office recalled the file. For tax refund and disposal, the GST field officer prepared a report and sent it to Deputy Commissioner Ambika Singh. Demanded ₹50K bribe for approval Deputy Commissioner Ambika called Ajay to the office for file disposal and asked questions related to tax. She sought clarification based on the report, then instead of disposing of the file, she talked about rejecting it. When Ajay pleaded to approve it, Ambika Singh demanded a bribe of 50 thousand rupees. When Ajay refused to pay the bribe, Ambika threatened action. After much struggle, Ajay agreed to pay 50 thousand rupees. However, Ajay went straight from the GST office to vigilance office. There, he narrated the entire matter to the SP. Arrest made at Dada Restaurant On Ajay Maurya's complaint, Varanasi's Anti-Corruption Team conducted an investigation. The allegations were confirmed in this. After this, preparations were made to take action against Ambika. On Wednesday at 6:30 PM, Ajay called Ambika Singh to Dada Restaurant to take ₹50K. Ambika Singh took the envelope of notes inside the restaurant and started to leave. Just then, the vigilance team caught her red-handed. Pleaded to be saved from the crowd As soon as she was caught red-handed, Ambika tried to flee, but 4 women inspectors caught her. On this, Ambika also scuffled with those women inspectors, but could not escape from their clutches. During this, Ambika pleaded with the crowd gathered around to save her. The woman officer kept telling passersby that she was being wrongly framed, but no one came to help. The team has registered a case under bribery sections. Now other files approved by Ambika Singh will also be investigated. Meanwhile, after the arrest, a case has been registered against Ambika Singh at the Vigilance police station in Varanasi. The Vigilance has clarified that action against corruption will continue. The department has appealed to people that if any public servant demands a bribe in exchange for government work, they should lodge a complaint on the department's helpline numbers - 9454401866 or 9454401222.

stories.title: Bulldozers set to roll at Azam Khan's Jauhar university:Rampur DM gives 15-day deadline to demolish structures or face action
stories.summary: Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, belonging to former UP minister and Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan, will be demolished. On Wednesday, District Magistrate Ajay Kumar Dwivedi rejected the university management's arguments after a hearing. Following this, the Rampur Development Authority (RDA) has initiated its action. In the RDA's investigation, out of a total of 40 buildings constructed on the university campus, only two were found to have approved maps, while 38 buildings were built without maps. On this basis, the authority had issued a notice to the university management seeking clarification. Regarding the matter, DM Ajay Kumar Dwivedi stated, As per rules, the institution is given 15 days to remove this illegal construction themselves. And if this does not happen, the RDA will take action itself and remove this illegal construction. He further said, Azam Khan and his son Abdullah Azam have been imprisoned in Rampur jail since November 17, 2025. They were sentenced to 7 years by Rampur's special MP-MLA court in a case of possessing two PAN cards. Azam's wife Tanzeen Fatima is out on bail. Authority issued notice seeking explanation The Rampur Development Authority (RDA) issued a notice to Jauhar University on July 1, 2026, asking it to submit documents if it had any valid building permissions or approved layout plans for its structures. In response, the university administration said the buildings were constructed before the Rampur Development Authority came into existence, so their plans could not be approved by the RDA. The District Magistrate rejected this argument and gave the university management another opportunity to present its case in person. During Wednesday's hearing, the university's Deputy Registrar repeated the same explanation. The District Magistrate clarified that the District Panchayat had jurisdiction over the area at the time, and approvals for two university buildings had been obtained from that authority. He said this showed the management was aware of the legal requirements, and failing to obtain approval for the remaining buildings amounted to a violation of the rules. After the hearing, the RDA began preparing action against the buildings declared unauthorised. Demolition orders may be issued soon. DM: University failed to justify unapproved buildings District Magistrate Ajay Kumar Dwivedi said Jauhar University is located in Singankhera village. The area came under the jurisdiction of the Rampur Development Authority in 2024; before that, it was under the District Panchayat. He said building plans for two university structures had been approved by the District Panchayat, proving that the university management was fully aware of the approval process. However, the remaining 38 buildings were constructed without obtaining the required permissions. The DM added that after the RDA took over the area in 2024, it also assumed the District Panchayat's responsibilities related to building approvals and action against illegal constructions, including demolition. How was Jauhar University established and controversies around it? Azam formed Jauhar trust in 2003; CM Mulayam Singh attended foundation ceremony with entire cabinet Azam Khan founded the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust in 2003, the year he was appointed Minister for Parliamentary Affairs, Urban Development, Employment, Water Supply and Poverty Alleviation in the Mulayam Singh Yadav government. This period marked the beginning of his political dominance in Rampur. Members of Azam Khan's family were also included in the trust. In 2005, Azam Khan decided to establish Mohammad Ali Jauhar University under the trust, with the aim of making it one of Uttar Pradesh's largest educational institutions. On September 18, 2005, then Chief Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav, accompanied by his entire cabinet, visited Rampur to lay the foundation stone of the university. As construction of the university began, it also became the centre of several controversies. It was alleged that 35 bighas of land belonging to 26 farmers in Aliyaganj village, Rampur, were acquired without their consent and purchased at throwaway prices for the project. Most of these developments took place between 2005 and 2007 during the Mulayam Singh government, and later between 2012 and 2015 under the Akhilesh Yadav government. Critics alleged that when local residents protested, they were falsely implicated in cases such as theft of construction materials and damaging university property, and were subsequently jailed. By 2017, the university had started offering 25 courses, including BA, BSc, BTech and BPharm. To support these programmes, 58 separate buildings were constructed on the campus. During the Samajwadi Party government, the Labour Department estimated the cost of these buildings at around ₹2,000 crore. University built across 1,500 bighas Akhilesh Yadav government left office in March 2017, after which Yogi Adityanath became Chief Minister. Following the BJP's return to power, Jauhar University began facing a series of legal and administrative actions. Of the 90 cases registered against Azam Khan in Rampur, 30 are related to Jauhar University. The university is spread over around 1,500 bighas of land. The acquisition of land for the campus remains the subject of ongoing legal disputes. Authorities have been taking action against the university continuously for the past seven years.

stories.title: RPF commandant suddenly salutes Modi, Shah in Agra:'Won't bow to pressure,' he says over Railway officer assault
stories.summary: RPF Senior Commandant Rajmohan Pichai held a press conference on Wednesday at 2 PM in Agra, regarding the assault case of a railway officer three days ago. First, Pichai stood up from his seat and saluted PM Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnav, and the Director General of the department. After this, he said that Violence is not right under any circumstances. Action will not be taken based on what is going viral on social media. I will not come under pressure. Action will be taken not emotionally, but based on documents. Nowadays, anyone can spread anything for money. Commandant said- Our personnel were doing their duty Senior Commandant Rajmohan Pichai clarified before starting his statement that he is from Tamil Nadu and his Hindi is not that good. On the railway station incident, he said- Violence is not right under any circumstances, but at the time this incident occurred, the RPF personnel were performing their duty completely according to the rules. It is worth thinking about what happened that made them agitated. He informed that there was a significant crowd on the platform on the day of the incident. RPF personnel were fulfilling their responsibility of passenger safety and safe train operations. During this time, a dispute arose regarding a passenger, and the matter escalated. Physical altercation with any officer or employee is not acceptable; therefore, action has also been taken against the concerned RPF personnel. Know the officer's 4 major points Decisions taken emotionally can be wrong: In today's era, any information or video can be made viral on a large scale. In such a situation, it would not be appropriate to make decisions based solely on content circulating on social media. No action will be taken under pressure from what is going on in the media or social media. After the investigation is complete, decisions will be made based on the facts and documents that come to light. Decisions taken emotionally can be wrong. The RPF officer said, It is not right to make decisions under emotional pressure in any matter. He said that action will be taken according to rules and procedures. There is a higher possibility of a decision being wrong if taken emotionally. Therefore, the department is proceeding based on facts and evidence. We do not support what the personnel did: We are not saying that the behavior of the RPF personnel was correct. Not one, but four personnel were involved in the incident, and the matter is being investigated. Whatever happened, we are not supporting it. All aspects are being investigated, and action will be taken in accordance with the guidelines of the Railway Ministry and senior officers. Allegations against RPF baseless: Dismissing allegations of taking money to conduct operations against RPF, he said that the department works impartially. It is wrong to say that RPF takes money to work. Rules and responsibility are paramount for us. No decision will be taken under any kind of pressure. At this time, the investigation is still ongoing, so CCTV footage cannot be made public for now. All facts will be presented after the investigation is complete. Law and order will not be allowed to be affected by the incident, and railway services will continue to operate normally. Security commissioner says, ‘Passenger safety is our priority’ The Senior Divisional Security Commissioner said- Railways are the lifeline of the country and ensuring passenger safety is the primary responsibility of RPF. He said that all facts related to the incident will be impartially investigated and an appropriate decision will be taken. Our job is to run trains, not to stop them. Whatever steps are taken will be based on rules and investigation reports. Know the Complete Matter On the morning of July 12 at Agra Cantt Railway Station, a dispute between Deputy Station Superintendent (DSS) Narendra Chahar and RPF personnel escalated into a physical altercation. According to information, during the departure of the Amritsar-Hirakud Express from Platform No. 1, a female passenger had alighted from the train to purchase goods. When the train started moving, she attempted to board it while running. Considering the passenger's safety, DSS Narendra Chahar informed the loco pilot via walkie-talkie and stopped the train. When the train's speed reduced, the woman started boarding, but an RPF jawan stationed there stopped her on charges of chain pulling. Narendra Chahar intervened and informed that he had stopped the train, but an argument broke out between them over this matter. It is alleged that when the dispute escalated, the RPF jawan called his colleagues and four jawans together caught hold of Narendra Chahar. When he protested, he was thrown to the ground and dragged approximately 300 meters by holding his hands and feet. However, the RPF jawans allege that Narendra Chahar had behaved indecently and abused them, after which the dispute escalated.

stories.title: 'She avoided me, so I killed her':Pilibhit medical student's murder accused says, 'I couldn't bear her liking someone else'
stories.summary: "I loved Kashish, but she kept avoiding me. I tried hard to convince her, but she refused. I couldn't bear the thought of her liking someone else, so I killed her." This is the confession of Sagar Singh, the accused in the murder of Kashish, a paramedical student at Pilibhit Medical College. On July 14, Sagar, her classmate, allegedly stabbed Kashish multiple times inside the medical college campus, killing her over one-sided love. During police interrogation, Sagar said, "Four days earlier, I bought a 12-inch knife from the market. I was waiting for the right opportunity to kill her. On Tuesday, I found her alone in the CT scan room. I first tried to persuade her, but she started shouting. I then took the knife out of my bag and stabbed her several times in the chest and abdomen." See two photos… Kashish, a 20-year-old student from Bareilly, was allegedly murdered by her classmate, Sagar Singh, at around 9:30 am on Tuesday. The incident took place inside the CT scan room of Pilibhit Medical College, where Kashish was present. According to police, the two first had an argument, after which Sagar pulled a knife from his bag and attacked her repeatedly. Kashish tried to run for her life, but Sagar chased her, caught hold of her, and stabbed her multiple times in the chest and abdomen. A female staff member who tried to intervene was also injured in the attack. Both were initially admitted to the medical college hospital but were later referred to Shri Ram Murti Smarak Institute of Medical Sciences (SRMS), Bareilly, as their condition was critical. Kashish succumbed to her injuries during treatment at around 2 pm. The injured staff member is still undergoing treatment. The news of Kashish's death left her family devastated. Her mother broke down repeatedly and fainted several times in grief. After the post-mortem examination was completed later in the evening, Kashish's final rites were performed. Accused says, 'I tried everything to convince her' During police interrogation, Sagar, a resident of Medua village in Kanpur's Araul police station area, said, "I was trying to convince her. For about a week, I kept trying to meet her. She would always leave with her friends and ignored me whenever she saw me. I couldn't bear it anymore, so I decided to kill her. Four days ago, I bought a knife from the market. During those four days, I didn't speak to her but kept following her." He further told police, "I couldn't sleep properly during those four days. I kept thinking about her all the time. Sometimes, I hoped she would agree, and then I wouldn't do anything. But if she refused, I had decided I wouldn't spare her." Sagar added, “On Tuesday, I found her alone in the CT scan room. I went up to her and tried to talk, but she refused even to look at me. I lost my temper, pulled out the knife, and when she tried to run, I chased her down and stabbed her multiple times.” Uncle says, ‘Complaint filed against Sagar 15 days ago’ Kashish's father, Rohatas, who works as a driver, and her uncle, Vikas Patel, reached Pilibhit on Wednesday morning. They met District Magistrate Gyanendra Singh and SP Sukirti Madhav Mishra, demanding strict punishment for Sagar. Vikas Patel said Sagar was obsessed with Kashish and had been harassing her for a long time. "About 15 days ago, we lodged a complaint with the medical college administration, but no action was taken. That emboldened him, and he went on to commit this horrific crime," he alleged. Uncle: 'Sagar destroyed everything' Vikas Patel said, "The case should be heard in a fast-track court. We will accept nothing less than the death penalty for the accused. My niece would have completed her education and become the family's support, but Sagar destroyed everything." Kashish's father- We were first told she had been injured Kashish's father, Rohatas, said the family was initially informed on Tuesday morning that his daughter had been injured. Accused's Sister: He had returned to the village for NEET exam Sagar's sister, Preeti, said, "After passing Class 12, my brother had been pursuing an X-ray technician course in Pilibhit for the past year. About a month ago, he came back to the village to appear for the NEET examination. He stayed for a day before returning to Pilibhit." Mother: We had no idea about any relationship Sagar's mother, Maya Devi, said, "My son never mentioned any love affair to the family. Had I known, I would have explained things to him and called him back home. We have daughters too, and so do others. No one should have to lose a daughter like this." She said the family learned about the incident at around 10 am. "A faculty member from the medical college first called my daughter, who then informed me about the entire incident." Sagar's father, Ram Avtar, works as a mason. His elder brother, Tej Singh, is a driver. He has three sisters. The eldest is married, Preeti works in the medical field, and the youngest, Anshika, is studying to become an ANM. City Kotwali SHO Pramendra Kumar said: "Based on a complaint filed by the victim's father, a murder case has been registered against accused Sagar Singh, and he has been arrested. The 12-inch knife used in the crime has also been recovered. Further legal proceedings are underway."

stories.title: Cabinet approves Varanasi elevated corridors:Two 89 km routes planned; 1-hour journey to reduce to 20 minutes
stories.summary: The Central Government's Cabinet has approved two major road projects worth approximately ₹25,445.96 crores for Varanasi. Under these projects, two elevated corridors totaling 89.26 kilometers in length will be developed in the city. The government claims that this will reduce traffic congestion, halve travel time, and make access to religious, educational, and industrial areas much easier than before. 43.21 km long elevated corridor to be built along Varuna River The Cabinet has approved a 43.218 kilometer long 6/4 lane elevated corridor along the Varuna River. This project will be developed on the Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) and its estimated cost will be ₹10,998.32 crores. This project is considered an important part of the Varanasi De-Congestion plan. Its construction will provide direct and fast connectivity between NH-31 and Kashi Railway Station. The journey that currently takes approximately 40 minutes will be reduced to about 20 minutes. Additionally, the project will improve access to Chandauli Social Economic Zone, a social node, and six major logistics hubs, which is expected to boost economic activities in the region. 46 km greenfield corridor to be built from NH-19 to ring road The Cabinet has also approved a 46.039-kilometer-long 6-lane greenfield elevated corridor between NH-19 and Varanasi Ring Road. ₹14,447.64 crore will be spent on this project. Once the corridor is built, seamless connectivity will be established between NH-19 and the Ring Road. This will reduce pressure on the city's existing road network and make urban traffic smoother. According to government estimates, after completion of this project, the average travel time in the area will reduce from 60 minutes to approximately 20 minutes. This will make access easier to Kashi Vishwanath Dham, major ghats, educational institutions, and cultural sites. Relief from traffic jams, boost to tourism and trade After the completion of both projects, the traffic system in Varanasi is expected to get a new direction. Connectivity between the city's inner and outer areas will be strengthened, which will greatly benefit devotees, tourists, students, and people involved in business activities. Experts believe that these projects will not only reduce traffic pressure but will also strengthen Varanasi as a major religious, cultural, and economic center of Purvanchal. What is the Ganga Elevated Corridor? The Ganga Elevated Corridor will be a six-lane elevated road running parallel to the Ganga River. Its length will be approximately 46 kilometers. It will connect National Highway-19 (NH-19) to the Varanasi Ring Road. Through this corridor, access to Assi Ghat, Manikarnika Ghat, Namo Ghat, and Kashi Vishwanath Dham will become easier. After the construction of this project, travel time between several parts of Varanasi is expected to reduce significantly. The most special feature of this project will be that it will be designed in such a way that the natural form of the Ganges River and the ghats is not harmed. It also proposes the construction of a cable-stayed bridge, meaning a bridge supported by cables. Additionally, viewpoints and viewing galleries will be built for tourists, from where people can see the beautiful view of the Ganges and the ghats. There is also a plan to build three pedestrian suspension bridges to cross the Ganges.

stories.title: Major fire in 4-storey building in Noida, 2 burnt alive:50 families rescued through ladders; fire triggered after blast during scooter charging
stories.summary: A fire broke out in a five-storey residential building in Noida on Wednesday afternoon, killing two people and leaving a child and a young woman critically injured. According to the police's preliminary investigation, an electric scooter was being charged on the ground floor when it exploded, triggering the blaze. The fire spread rapidly through the building, burning several motorcycles parked inside. Seven fire engines were rushed to the spot. More than 100 people from around 50 families living in the building were rescued. Videos from the scene show ladders placed between the rooftops of two adjacent buildings, allowing residents to escape safely. Police have taken the building owner into custody for questioning. The incident occurred in the Mamura area of Sector 66, a densely populated neighbourhood where many working professionals live with their families. See pictures Follow our live blog for the latest updates on the fire incident…..

stories.title: Former PPN College chairman dies by suicide:He shot himself in the head; wife lives separately with daughters in Lucknow
stories.summary: The former president of PPN College in Kanpur has shot himself to death with a licensed gun. On Wednesday morning, family members broke down his room door and brought out the body. Upon examination, a bullet wound was found in the head. Police did not find any suicide note in the room. Initial investigation revealed that Alok Singh's (50) wife was living separately with their daughters in Lucknow, due to which he was under stress and had started drinking alcohol. Father narrates the entire incident Keshav Nath Singh, a resident of Basant Vihar W-2, lived in a two-story house with his three sons Ajit, Alok, and Abhay. Keshav Nath said, “On Tuesday evening, Alok returned home from work. After having dinner, he closed the door of his room and went to sleep with the AC on." He worked in the transport business with his father Keshav Nath said, "My transport business operates from Morang Mandi. My son Alok also helped in the transport work. In 2021, during the coronavirus pandemic, my elder son Ajit Singh passed away." Elder daughter in Merchant Navy, younger one studying in 12th Keshav Nath said Alok's wife is Vinita, and he has two daughters, Anushka and Anshika. Anushka is in the Merchant Navy, while Anshika is studying Intermediate in Lucknow. Two years ago, Vinita's father had arranged a flat for them in Lucknow. Station in-charge Rajeev Kumar said that during interrogation, family members said that on Tuesday evening, a blast sound was heard, but they did not pay attention to it. The body has been sent for post-mortem. Daughters reach home after father's death Alok Singh's two daughters reached home at around 3 pm after being informed of their father's death. His father, Keshav Nath, said, “I spoke to my son just two days ago. Everything seemed fine. I don't know what happened. There were never any quarrels in our family.” Station House Officer Rajeev Kumar said: "The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination. Further action will be taken after the investigation. During questioning, it emerged that Alok had been under stress. Police are investigating the death from all possible angles."

stories.title: Atal Medical University convocation:Over 11,000 students receive degrees; MBBS courses and affordable treatment announced
stories.summary: The second convocation ceremony of Atal Bihari Vajpayee Medical University (ABVMU) was held on Wednesday. Degrees in MBBS, MD, MS, nursing and paramedical courses were awarded to 11,053 students from across Uttar Pradesh. A total of 32 meritorious students received gold medals, while 25 were awarded silver medals. Governor Anandiben Patel presented medals to 25 toppers on stage. On the occasion, Vice-Chancellor Dr Amit Devgan said that ABVMU will no longer remain limited to affiliating medical, nursing and paramedical institutions. "The university will soon establish its own medical college, where MBBS courses will be introduced. It will also provide quality healthcare at affordable rates to the public," Devgan said. Presently, ABVMU does not have its own medical college. It is only affiliated with medical colleges.

stories.title: Ram Mandir donation theft:Police question two accused on how the money was stolen hidden; 1,000 apply for CEO post in 24 hours
stories.summary: Police have taken Ramashankar Mishra and retired banker Subhash Srivastava, both accused in the Ayodhya Ram Mandir donation theft case, into 14-hour custody for questioning. On Wednesday at 8 am, officers reached Faizabad Jail and brought both men to police lines. After interrogation, they may also be taken to their homes. Police will investigate how the accused allegedly stole the donation money and where they hid it. Ramashankar was responsible for transporting the offerings to the counting room. Investigators have found ₹7.32 lakh in his bank account. Subhash, a retired State Bank of India (SBI) employee, supervised those counting the donations. On Tuesday, police produced Ramashankar and Subhash Srivastava before the court and sought seven days' custody, but the court granted only 14 hours' police remand. Earlier, police had questioned co-accused Avinash Shukla, Anukalp Mishra, Lavkush Mishra and Karunesh Pandey. Meanwhile, the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust is preparing to return offerings to devotees who had raised concerns over the safety of donated valuables. Donors alleged they had offered gold and silver jewellery and other valuable items to Ram Lalla but were not issued receipts, leading to doubts about whether their offerings were being kept securely. According to sources, more than 1,000 applications have been received from across the country for the post of CEO of the Ram Mandir. The selection committee received the applications on its official email within 24 hours of the recruitment notification being issued. The highest number of applicants are retired government officials.

stories.title: Non-veg banned in Lucknow's KGMU hostels:SP calls it a 'Tughlaqi diktat', asks if BJP MPs who eat fish and rice will face similar orders
stories.summary: Politics has erupted over the ban on non-vegetarian food in the hostels of King George Medical University (KGMU) in Lucknow. Samajwadi Party spokesperson Fakhrul Hasan Chand said on Wednesday, "This order is a Tughlaqi decree. Will Governor Anandiben Patel issue any order for those BJP MPs who eat fish and rice in Bengal? Your ideology only changes after coming to UP." Maulana Khalid Rasheed Firangi Mahali, Imam of Lucknow Eidgah, said, "The KGMU administration should withdraw its decision. More than 61 per cent of people in India are non-vegetarian. From a medical perspective, non-vegetarian food is considered beneficial for human health." Meanwhile, Shia cleric Maulana Yasoob Abbas said: It is the university's decision. No one needs to comment on it. If someone wants to eat non-vegetarian food, they can go outside and eat it. This should not be linked to politics. Meanwhile, BJP MP Dinesh Sharma said, “The university itself decides what kind of food will be given to the students. If most students prefer a particular type of food, the institution can make arrangements accordingly. This should not be made a subject of controversy.” Protein-rich vegetarian food should be given instead of non-veg KGMU's Chief Provost Prof. Kamal Kumar Sawlani issued an order on Tuesday regarding the ban on non-vegetarian food in the mess and canteen of 18 hostels. He said, “Now, non-vegetarian food will neither be cooked nor served in the mess and canteen. To ensure students get sufficient protein, vegetarian protein-rich food items should be included in their meals. This order should be implemented with immediate effect.”

stories.title: Fake IAS woman's husband says 'she tried to strangle me':Married after seeing officer-like photos on Facebook, says 'ruined my life'
stories.summary: 'I was told that the girl is an IAS officer. A case is going on in court; as soon as the decision comes, she will get the joining (letter). Then she will also get me a government job. The family thought that the family's fortune would change, but just a few days after the wedding, it was found that everything was a lie.' This is what Abhishek Singh, a resident of Faridpur in Bareilly, says. In conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, Abhishek claimed that he was married after being deceived into believing the girl was an IAS officer. After marriage, the wife put pressure on the family by calling herself an officer. She took jewellery and money, put pressure to sell land. “When we refused, she threatened to trap us in false cases,” Abhishek said. Now in this case, the police have arrested the wife, Sadhana Singh (fake IAS) and sent her to jail. However, Sadhana's maternal family has called all the allegations baseless. The father says that the truth will come out in court. Now hear the complete story from husband Abhishek Singh... Facebook photos built trust Abhishek says - The marriage proposal came through relatives. The girl's family claimed that Sadhana had been selected for IAS. She will get the appointment after a pending court case is resolved. They also said that after getting the job, she will help me get a government job too. I checked her Facebook. There were photos in IAS officer-like clothes and from government events. We became fully convinced that she was telling the truth. She said I am an IAS officer, I won't do household work Abhishek said, "After the wedding on February 7, 2025, Sadhana's behaviour completely changed. She would not do any household work. When her mother asked her, she would say that I am an IAS officer; I won't do any work. If you trouble me too much, I will send everyone to jail. Sadhana beat up my father. After this, he had to leave home and go to my sister's place. She took back the four lakh rupees given in the tilak, saying that a big car would be given to the daughter. Later, a Bolero was purchased on finance. But, the very next day after the wedding, Sadhana said that her instalments would be paid by the in-laws. Pressure to open a hospital for brother; demanded 20 lakhs Abhishek said - I have done D-Pharma. Sadhana told me to give 20 lakh rupees. My brother is a doctor; we will get a hospital built. You can run a medical store. Sadhana took about 15 tolas of gold, one and a half kilos of silver and other jewellery received in the wedding, citing expenses for becoming an IAS officer and court cases. Later, she started pressuring to sell 20 bighas of land in the name of building a hospital in Badaun. Tried to kill me by strangling my neck at night Abhishek said, "One night in March 2026, Sadhana tried to kill me by strangling me while I was sleeping. I called Dial-112 and summoned the police. Later, a panchayat was held in the village, where she assured that she would return the jewellery. However, that did not happen. Meanwhile, I went to Badaun court several times with Sadhana. There it was revealed that the case which was being claimed to be related to IAS appointment was actually an old lawsuit related to the IT Act. After this, I realised that I had been cheated. Police said - Created fake IAS image on Facebook According to police, during interrogation Sadhana admitted that she had posted fake photos and videos on Facebook to portray herself as an IAS officer. She also admitted to asking her husband to sell land to build a hospital and demanding 40 lakh rupees during the dispute. In the FIR registered at Faridpur police station, besides Sadhana Singh, a case has also been registered against her father Narendrapal Singh, brother Surya Pratap and relative Rajendra Singh. SP South Anshika Verma said- A case was registered on June 27, 2026, based on Abhishek's complaint. Based on investigation and available evidence, Sadhana Singh was arrested on July 13. After being presented in court, Sadhana was sent to jail. Sadhana's parents called the allegations false Sadhana's parents have denied all allegations. They say that their daughter has been trapped in a false case. They claim that Sadhana is meritorious in studies. The truth of the entire matter will come out in court.

stories.title: Storm, rain lash Ayodhya; Bhakti Path submerged under one-foot water:Yamuna swells in Mathura; rain alert in 33 cities
stories.summary: The monsoon has weakened across Uttar Pradesh, with most parts of the state receiving little to no rain. Around 2 am on Wednesday, Ayodhya witnessed rain accompanied by strong winds, leading to waterlogging on roads. Devotees visiting the temple were seen wading through knee-deep water. Lucknow also received rain late night on Tuesday, with light showers continuing intermittently in several areas until Wednesday morning. Agra, Mathura, Noida, Ghaziabad and several other cities remain under cloudy skies with brief spells of sunshine. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 33 districts on Wednesday. Meanwhile, continuous rainfall in the hill states has caused river levels to rise across Uttar Pradesh. In Mathura, the Yamuna is in spate and is flowing 1.30 metres below the warning level. The steps at Keshi Ghat in Vrindavan have been submerged. The Ramganga in Bareilly and the Malan river in Bijnor are also nearing the danger mark. In Prayagraj, the Ganga and Yamuna have reached shops built along the ghats. In Kanpur, the Ganga's water level has risen by 20 cm, with water reaching the steps of Anandeshwar Temple Ghat. Riverbank erosion has begun along the Saryu and Ghaghara rivers in Ballia. In Bansdih, around 150 families have left their homes and relocated to safer areas. Rain-bearing clouds disappear from 80% of the state According to the IMD, dry winds from Pakistan have pushed rain-bearing clouds away from nearly 80% of Uttar Pradesh, weakening monsoon activity. The impact is already visible. Only 11 cities recorded rainfall on Tuesday. Against an expected average of 9.7 mm, the state received just 1.5 mm of rain. Between 1 June and 14 July, Uttar Pradesh received 163.1 mm of rainfall, which is 22 per cent below the seasonal average.

stories.title: Railways revise 13 rules:Heavier penalties for ticketless travel, entering ladies' coaches and smoking; on-the-spot fines introduced
stories.summary: The Railways has made changes to 13 rules. Now littering on trains or railway stations, traveling without a ticket, boarding ladies' coaches, or creating a disturbance while intoxicated will be costly. In such cases, RPF and TTE will collect fines on the spot. The matter will end there upon paying the fine, but if the penalty is not paid, one can be presented in court. One can even be sent to jail. Know the rules that have been changed Under section 137 of the Railway Act, 1989, if any person knowingly travels on a train without a ticket, with a wrong ticket, or with a previously used ticket, they will have to pay the full fare for the distance traveled. If it cannot be determined where they started their journey, the railway will collect the fare from the station where the train departed or where the ticket was checked. Additionally, a penalty equal to the fare will also have to be paid, which will be a minimum of ₹500. Cannot occupy someone else's seat Under section 155, forcibly sitting on a reserved seat or berth of a passenger is punishable. If any passenger does so or refuses to vacate the seat, a fine shall be imposed on the spot. If you dirty the train-station, you will have to pick up the garbage Littering, spitting, creating a ruckus after drinking alcohol or misbehaving with passengers at train-stations will now prove costly. Under section 145 of the Railway Act, 1989, a fine of ₹1,000 will have to be paid immediately in such cases. Along with this, the offender will also have to perform '24 hours of community service'. This may include tasks such as- If any passenger habitually litters or creates nuisance even after warning, the matter will be considered serious. Then the court can impose six months imprisonment, fine up to ₹5,000 or both punishments. Illegal entry into ladies coach will be a ₹5,000 fine Entering a coach, cabin, seat, berth or waiting room reserved for women will prove costly for male passengers. If a man knowingly does so or does not leave even after being told by railway staff, his ticket can be confiscated. Additionally, an on-the-spot fine of ₹2,500 will be imposed under section 162 of the Railway Act, 1989. If he refuses to pay the fine, the matter will go to court. If found guilty there, a fine of up to ₹5,000 can be imposed. Even in normal circumstances, the court will not impose a fine less than ₹2,500. However, this provision will not apply to transgenders. Action will not be taken against them under this section. Dangerous items will be confiscated if carried on trains Carrying flammable, explosive, poisonous or other dangerous goods on trains is banned. If any passenger breaks railway rules, their entire luggage will be confiscated. Along with this, if that luggage causes damage to the railway or any passenger, compensation will also have to be paid. Under Section 164 of the Railway Act, 1989, the minimum fine will be ₹10,000. If the damage is more, the fine can also increase accordingly. If the accused refuses to pay the fine or remove the luggage, the case will go to court. If found guilty there, punishment can be up to 1 year imprisonment, minimum ₹10,000 fine or both. If you carry excess luggage, railway will collect charges Earlier, a fine of up to ₹500 per 100 kg could be imposed for carrying luggage beyond the prescribed limit. This will not happen now. Under section 165, the central government will notify the fine amount from time to time. This means the fine will no longer be a fixed amount. It will be collected according to the rates fixed by the government. Can Go to Jail for Entering No-Entry Area Under section 147 of the Railway Act, 1989, entering platforms and waiting areas without a valid ticket or pass is prohibited. Entry is also not allowed in railway tracks, yards, control rooms or signalling areas. If any person violates these rules, a fine of ₹2,000 will be immediately collected from them. Earlier, the maximum fine for this mistake was up to ₹500. If the accused person refuses to pay this fine on the spot or does not comply with the order to leave from there, the case will go to court. Then there can be imprisonment up to three months, fine up to ₹5,000 or both punishments. Illegal vending, selling goods and begging banned There will be a ban on selling goods without a licence, hawking, or begging at railway stations and on trains. Under section 144 of the Railway Act, 1989, a fine of ₹2,000 will be collected on the spot from such people. They will be released upon paying the fine. If someone refuses to pay the fine, the case will go to court. If found guilty there, they may face imprisonment of up to three months, a fine of up to ₹5,000, or both punishments. Meanwhile, strict action will be taken against repeat offenders. For being caught the fourth time, there is a provision for imprisonment of up to 1 year and a fine of up to ₹5,000.

stories.title: Railway DSS assault case:Passenger claims he was on Agra platform, falsely accused of chain-pulling
stories.summary: "On July 12, I was traveling to Puri on the Hirakund Express with my friend Ranjita. When the train stopped at Agra, we got down on the platform to buy petha. After some time, the train started moving. Ranjita had an injury on her foot, so she couldn't run. Seeing this, the Deputy Station Superintendent (DSS) helped us and stopped the train. Both of us boarded the train. “Just then, RPF personnel arrived. They made me and Ranjita get off the train. They were taking us to the police station. Then the Deputy SS said that he had stopped the train. The personnel started beating up the Deputy SS. They took ₹1,000 from me for the crime of chain pulling. They didn't even give a receipt. When we couldn't even board the train, how could we have pulled the chain?” This is what train passenger Ashish, a resident of Ludhiana, said. Deputy SS Narendra Chahar had stopped the train for Ashish's friend Ranjita. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Ashish over the phone. Ashish said that we had done nothing wrong. Yet we were treated like accused. Story of assault on railway officer, in passenger's words DSS helped us, RPF personnel forcibly dragged him away Ashish explains, “Ranjita and I were sitting in the M-1 coach of the Hirakund Express train. On Sunday (12 July) morning around 11 o'clock, the train stopped at Agra Cantt station. We both got down to buy petha. We were just paying for the petha when the train started moving. I ran to catch the train. But my friend Ranjita couldn't run fast because she had an injury on her foot.” “Seeing our train leaving, Deputy Station Superintendent Narendra Chahar, who was present on the platform, informed the loco pilot via walkie-talkie and stopped the train. After the train stopped, we both boarded the B-3 coach of the train. We had just sat down on our seats when RPF personnel came from behind. They made us get down from the train. They said that we both had pulled the chain. When we refused, they forcibly dragged us both to take us to the police station. Just then, Deputy SS Narendra Chahar arrived there. He told the personnel that Ashish and Ranjita did not stop the train. ‘Their train was leaving, so I informed the loco pilot and stopped the train.’ However, the RPF personnel were not ready to listen to him,” Ashish said. RPF personnel beat up and knocked DSS to the ground Ashish said, “An argument broke out between the RPF personnel and the Deputy SS. Then it came to blows between the two. Other people present on the platform also gathered. DSS Narendra Chahar's staff members also came. However, the RPF personnel did not listen to anyone.” “Ranjita was holding DSS Narendra Chahar's hand. She was continuously telling the RPF personnel that nothing like this had happened. Meanwhile, one personnel slapped DSS Narendra Chahar. Then other people also started beating DSS Narendra Chahar. They threw him down on the platform. The RPF team dragged the DSS to the RPF station. Four RPF personnel dragged him by holding his hands and feet for about 300 meters. People present at the station had made a video of this entire incident,” he said. When we were not on the train, how could we pull the chain? Ashish said, “RPF took me and Ranjita to the station. They took one ₹1,000 from us for the crime of chain pulling. They didn't give any receipt for it. Whereas, we had not pulled the chain. When we couldn't even board the train, we were not on the train, then how did we pull the chain? We told the RPF people this many times, but they didn't listen at all.” “Due to the dispute at the station, their train was missed. Both of us stayed at the station for quite some time. Then we left by another train. We have come to participate in the Jagannath Yatra,” he said. What came in the DSS' medical report? The medical report of Station Superintendent Narendra Singh Chahar came out on Tuesday (July 14). The examination by the ENT specialist at the district hospital confirmed the rupture of Narendra Chahar's left eardrum (tympanic membrane laceration). Wife said, “If no action is taken against the accused, I will give my life.” DSS Narendra Chahar's wife Harendri Chahar said on Tuesday, “You all know what those people did to my husband. It has been 3 days, but nothing has happened to those people. They did so much wrong, so much wrong that no one can watch that video. I haven't watched it yet. I can never tolerate this for my husband.” Protests were held across the state yesterday On Tuesday, protests were held across the state in the case of dragging and beating of a railway officer on the platform. From 10:30 AM, railway employees protested against RPF in 30 cities including Agra, Mathura, Jhansi. In Agra, more than 1,000 railway employees took to the streets. They raised slogans in front of RPF personnel outside the DRM office. Women employees also raised slogans of "RPF Murdabad" and "Shame-Shame". The sister of the victim railway officer had jumped onto the tracks. She had warned of stopping the train. Know what action has been taken so far What was the entire matter? At Agra Cantt Railway Station on the morning of July 12 (Sunday) around 11 AM, RPF personnel assaulted Deputy Station Superintendent Narendra Chahar. The Amritsar to Hirakud Express train had arrived at Platform Number-1. During this time, a female passenger got down from the same train and started buying some items. Just then the train started moving. The female passenger tried to board the moving train but could not get on. Deputy SS Narendra Chahar, who was stationed at the station, saw the woman running and informed the loco pilot via walkie-talkie and stopped the train. When the train's speed reduced, the woman started boarding it. Just then, the RPF personnel stationed there stopped the woman on charges of chain pulling. DSS Narendra Chahar protested against this. He said that he had stopped the train. However, the RPF personnel did not listen to him. A dispute arose between the two. It came to the point of physical altercation. The RPF jawan called his colleagues. All of them caught DSS Narendra Chahar and started taking him away. When he protested, they caught him and threw him on the ground. The DSS kept writhing on the floor. However, four RPF personnel kept dragging him by his hands and feet for about 300 meters. The RPF jawans alleged that the DSS had misbehaved with them using abusive language.

stories.title: How much time does Lucknow–Kanpur expressway actually save?:Journey gets completed in 44 minutes, but reaching Kanpur city takes 1 hour 47 minutes
stories.summary: Can the distance from Lucknow to Kanpur now be covered in 45 minutes? The government's claim was that the expressway would save a lot of time. When the expressway opened for the public on Tuesday, Dainik Bhaskar investigated the reality of whether one can actually reach Kanpur from Lucknow in 45 minutes. We started our journey at 10:19 AM from Indira Gandhi Pratishthan in Gomti Nagar of Lucknow. When we left by car, we had to stop for about 30 seconds at the first red light. After this, we proceeded towards Shaheed Path. In this part of the city, the average speed remained around 50 km per hour. We also encountered three to four minutes of traffic on the way. This was the reason we could cross Shaheed Path at 10:46 AM. That means it took 37 minutes to reach here from Indira Gandhi Pratishthan. From Amausi Airport, we headed towards the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway. At 11:03 AM, we reached the entry point of the expressway. It took 44 minutes to reach the expressway from Indira Gandhi Pratishthan. This is where the most important part of our journey began. Toll deducted from moving vehicle, surveillance with AI cameras After getting on the expressway, the first toll plaza came, but there was neither a barrier here nor did the vehicle have to be stopped. Cameras and FASTag readers installed about 500 meters before the toll plaza read the number plate and FASTag of the moving vehicle and deducted the toll money. The Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway is the country's first barrier-free expressway. On this expressway, our vehicle's average speed was around 100 km per hour. Due to wide roads and no traffic, the vehicle was moving smoothly at a consistent speed. Only a few vehicles were visible on the expressway. Throughout the expressway, emergency calling booths have been set up at various places, which are directly connected to the control room. In case of any incident or emergency situation, help will be dispatched immediately from here. CCTV cameras, signboards at regular intervals, and strong fencing on both sides were also visible on the road. During the journey, several bikes were also seen on this expressway. However, bikes are not permitted on this expressway. 6 interchanges for entry and exit A total of 6 interchanges have been built on the expressway. Towards Lucknow, interchanges are at Shaheed Path, Main Toll, Bani and Harouni, Ajgain and Amarsaas in Unnao, while towards Kanpur, an interchange has been built near Azad Chowk. From these locations, you can easily enter and exit the expressway. After completing the journey of approximately 63 kilometers on the expressway, we reached Azad Chowk, the ending point of the expressway, at 11:48 AM. It took us exactly 44 minutes to reach here from the entry point of the expressway. But the journey didn't end here. The entry point of Kanpur city is Rama Devi Chauraha. It is about 7 kilometers away from the expressway. It took us approximately 19 minutes to reach here. By this time, our vehicle had covered a distance of about 100 kilometers. We completed the entire journey from Indira Gandhi Pratishthan to Rama Devi Chauraha in 1 hour 47 minutes. Thus, our reality check revealed that the 63-kilometer expressway journey is being completed in 44 minutes. But it is taking about one and three-quarter hours to reach the starting points of both cities. Encountered barrier at toll while returning from Kanpur After stopping in Kanpur for a while, we started our return journey. At 2:15 PM, we headed towards Lucknow from Rama Devi Chowk. Shortly after getting on the expressway, the first control room appeared. The main toll plaza is near this. Here we saw a barrier at the toll. At some distance is the second control center, from where the entire expressway is monitored. AI-equipped advanced cameras have been installed here, which immediately detect any accident on the road, vehicle stoppage, wrong-way driving, or other unusual activities and send alerts to the control room. Food plaza and petrol pump not yet built Currently, facilities like food plaza and petrol pump are not available on the expressway. Land has been acquired for these and signboards have also been put up. However, no timeline has been fixed yet as to when these facilities will become available.

stories.title: Young scientist found dead at five-star hotel:Had come to Lucknow a day earlier; mother unconscious in shock
stories.summary: A 22-year-old scientist died in a five-star hotel in Lucknow. On Tuesday morning at 11 am, when the room door did not open, hotel staff informed the police. The police arrived at the scene, broke the door and entered to find the scientist's body on the bed. After examining the scene, the police and forensic team sent the body for post-mortem. Vomit was found under and around the dead body in the room. Food poisoning and heart attack are suspected to be the cause of death. The police are awaiting the post-mortem report. The scientist was a resident of Maharajganj district. His father is a farmer. The scientist had built an eco-friendly battery-operated tractor. His mother is in shock. She is repeatedly losing consciousness. The case is from Novotel in Vibhutikhand police station area. The scientist had checked into the hotel around 1:30 pm on Monday afternoon. ACP Vibhuti Khand Saumya Pandey said that when the police entered the room, Rahul's belongings were kept inside. The forensic team has collected evidence. See 3 pictures- Rahul was doing both research and studies Rahul Singh (22), a young scientist from Beejapaar Aasman Chhapra village in Siswa Bazaar, Maharajganj district, was a young scientist. Six years ago, when he was a 12th standard student at ABC Public School Divyanagar in Gorakhpur, he had made a battery-operated tractor. He was an innovator at the Design Innovator and Incubation Center of Madan Mohan Malaviya University of Technology. He was doing research and studies there. Rahul secured first place in the India International Science Festival for three consecutive years starting from the age of 13. In 2018, he made a roti maker, in 2019 a battery-operated eco-friendly bicycle, and in 2020, during the Coronavirus crisis, at the India International Science Festival held online, he made a battery-operated tractor. No need to charge the tractor's battery The tractor made by Rahul is completely eco-friendly. Since it runs on battery, it doesn't make any noise. As it doesn't use fuel (diesel-petrol), it is completely free from air pollution. This tractor, which runs at a speed of 70 kmph, can plow one acre of field in three hours. Rahul had also made its battery and motor himself. Rahul had mentioned that there is no need to charge its battery. It will keep charging itself as the tractor runs. Tractor has no gears, weighs one and a half quintals Rahul has also installed four indicators in the tractor. Along with this, it has two headlights, which will also help in plowing the field late in the evening. Along with this, he has installed power steering in it, which makes the tractor run smoothly. Also, a switch has been provided. By using this, the tractor can move forward or backward. Not only this, there is no need to change gears in this tractor. It is also very easy to drive. Its battery is placed in the front under the bonnet. Along with this, four fans are also installed inside to keep it cool. Its weight is around one and a half quintals.

stories.title: ₹7.32 lakh found in Ram Mandir donation theft accused's account:Ramashankar's family says 'saved salary'; Subhash's son says 'leave, or we'll call police'
stories.summary: Among the eight accused arrested in the Ram Mandir donation theft case are Ramashankar Mishra and Subhash Chandra Srivastava. A Dainik Bhaskar team reached both their homes and spoke with their families and neighbours. Ramashankar's family lives in two rooms at the Ram Sakha Bagiya temple in Ayodhya. Police found ₹7.32 lakh in his bank account. The family claims that this amount was accrued by saving from Ramashankar's salary. On the other hand, when we reached Subhash's house, his son refused to talk. Neighbours say that the family has not come out of the house since the arrest. Ramashankar's father is a priest at the temple, which is why they got two rooms to live in Ramashankar's family lives at Ram Sakha Bagiya Temple located in Meerapur, about 2 km away from Ram Temple. His father Chhaddu Lal Mishra has been conducting prayers here for the past 30 years. Due to this, he has been given two rooms to live in the temple premises. He also performs kirtan at a small temple near Hanumangarhi. The family consists of Ramashankar's parents, brother Vivek Shankar, sister-in-law Sadhana, their child, and one sister. Ramashankar studied up to 10th grade. About five years ago, he got a job at Ram Temple. Initially, he also earned money by taking photos of devotees visiting the temple. Later, his duty was assigned to deliver donation boxes to the counting place. Sister-in-law says, “Ramashankar never gave us even ₹10” Ramashankar's sister-in-law Sadhana said, "When the police took him away, they (police) searched the house. But, nothing was found. The police also checked our bank accounts and Aadhaar, nothing was found there either." She said, "Ramashankar never gave us even ₹10. When we needed money, he would instead take money from us. If he had stolen and brought money home, why would we still be living in 2 rooms today?" Sister said Ramashankar used to save his salary, expenses were managed from photography earnings Ramashankar's sister said that the family's financial condition has always been weak. “Father runs the household by doing kirtan. Many times he himself would buy and bring vegetables, so that his son wouldn't spend too much money,” she said. When asked about the ₹7.32 lakh found in the account, she said, "My brother had been working at Ram Mandir for the last five-six years. He used to get a salary of around 16,000 rupees per month. He would deposit his entire salary in the bank." Ramashankar's lifestyle had changed in the last one and a half years People in the neighborhood say that Ramashankar's lifestyle changed in the last one to one and a half years. He was often seen in new clothes and white towels. He spent most of his time with the other accused Anukalp, Avnish and Lavkush. For the past one and a half years, he was not living with his family. Even when his brother had an accident, he did not help, although he had lakhs of rupees in his account. The family members are also not clear about where he was staying. The police are now investigating the money that came into his bank accounts. Son said, “Leave from here, otherwise we will call the police.” Ram Mandir is about 5 kilometers away from Anjanipuram Colony where Subhash Chandra Srivastava's house is located. When the doorbell was rung, his son Rishabh asked, "Who is it?" Upon hearing the name of the media, he said, "You please leave from here, we will not talk. If you people don't leave, we will call the police." Claim of handling cash counting responsibility without salary Subhash Chandra Srivastava is a retired employee of State Bank of India. For the past one and a half years, he was in charge of counting the donation money at Ram Mandir. His responsibility was to supervise the counting of cash withdrawn from donation boxes and hand over the amount to SBI. He has been made an accused in the conspiracy for alleged irregularities in this process. People claimed that Subhash has been associated with RSS for a long time. After the Ram temple was built, he was handling this responsibility with a spirit of service without any salary. Embezzlement charges were leveled earlier too, job was restored by court People in the neighborhood say that Subhash is a person who minds his own business. During his job at SBI, he was once accused of embezzlement and was also suspended. However, later his job was restored by court order. If the charges had been proven, the court would not have reinstated him. Did not allow anyone to enter the counting room A person associated with counting the donation money at the temple said that after the counting of notes was completed, if someone entered the room, Subhash would scold them and throw them out. No one could enter without permission in his presence. Only that person would go inside whom Subhash himself called. Accused of conspiracy in preliminary investigation Among the 8 arrested people, no recovery has been made from Subhash alone. The allegation is that Subhash and Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu Yadav conspired to embezzle donation money in collusion with employees. The SIT's preliminary investigation report also mentions this. However, the complete picture will only become clear after the final report comes.

The written examination for the recruitment was conducted on 14th and 15th March 2026. Following the written examination, subsequent stages, and reservation rules, a total of 4,543 candidates have been finally selected. The recruitment board has uploaded the post-wise and category-wise selection list on its official website uppbpb.gov.in. Candidates can also check their final result through the link siupexam25.com/sifinalresults. Congratulating the selected candidates, the board said the normalised marks of all candidates who appeared for the written examination will be released on 22 July 2026. Candidates will be able to check their marks the same day through the link available on the board's official website.

stories.title: Fatwa issued over Aamir's third-marriage:UP mufti calls it invalid, says relationship with non-Muslim woman is a sin
stories.summary: A fatwa concerning Bollywood actor Aamir Khan's third marriage was issued in Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh, on Tuesday afternoon by Shahi Chief Mufti Maulana Chaudhary Ibrahim Hussain. The Mufti stated that, under Shariat (Islamic law), a Muslim man is not permitted to marry a non-Muslim woman who continues to follow her own religion and has not accepted Islam. He said such a marriage is considered invalid under Islamic law, and a Muslim man entering into it is regarded as committing a religious wrong. 2 pictures of Aamir-Gauri's wedding Karni Sena had accused Aamir of ‘love jihad’ Earlier on Tuesday itself, Thakur Gyanendra Singh, National Vice President of Kshatriya Karni Sena, said, ‘’At the age of 61, a common man retires and wants to live a comfortable life with his family. At that age, Aamir Khan has married a Hindu woman for the third time. He is promoting love jihad by marrying Hindu women every time. He is instigating Muslim youth for this. Thakur Gyanendra Singh had written a letter to the Shahi Chief Mufti asking whether this marriage is correct according to Islam. If this is wrong, then why doesn't Aamir Khan get the punishment that is prescribed for common Muslims? He had warned that the protest will continue until Aamir Khan is punished according to law and religion.'' Now, read what the Mufti said in response... Marriage without conversion is wrong: The Quran clearly states that until a non-Muslim woman accepts faith (i.e., accepts the Muslim religion), do not marry her. If a Muslim person knowingly marries a non-Muslim woman, that marriage will be religiously invalid. Nikah valid only upon accepting Quran and Prophet: The real meaning of a non-Muslim woman embracing faith is that she believes only in Allah. She accepts Hazrat Mohammad as the last Prophet (messenger). Besides this, she must have faith in the Quran and God's holy books. She must live life according to Islamic rules and practices. Deceiving first wife is a sin: Marrying a second time while keeping the first wife in deception is a grave sin. According to the Quran, if a person cannot treat his wives equally, cannot bear their expenses or fulfill their rights, then he is not permitted to marry more than once. Prophet Mohammad Sahab had said that the person who deceives is not one of us. Therefore, committing injustice with the first wife is a great sin. According to Islamic law, there is a difference between the two. Marriage with a Christian or Jewish woman is considered permissible after fulfilling certain necessary conditions. Marrying another non-Muslim woman without religious conversion is completely wrong. This is not a final verdict against any one person: The Mufti explained that this religious opinion (fatwa) that has been given is information about a general rule. This is not our final legal or court decision on Aamir Khan's or any particular person's private life. Karni Sena had asked us questions based on a letter, so we have only provided information about the general rules of Islam. The Mufti clarified what the ground reality is of Aamir Khan's third marriage. Whether that woman accepted Islam before marriage or not is a matter of investigation. The decision to directly declare any person guilty or to punish them can only be taken after examining all evidence and the actual status of the nikah. Aamir-Gauri's wedding took place on July 5 61-year-old Aamir Khan had a registered marriage with Gauri Spratt on July 5. Only a few close guests attended the wedding. After signing the wedding papers, the couple took their vows. During this, Aamir gave Gauri a priceless ring. First divorce happened in 2002 Aamir had his first marriage in 1986 with Reena Dutta. It was a love marriage that lasted for about 16 years. The two have two children, Junaid Khan and Ira Khan. In 2002, both legally separated. Second relationship with Kiran Rao, then separated by mutual consent After the divorce from Reena Dutta, director Kiran Rao came into Aamir Khan's life. Both got married in 2005. From this marriage, they have a son, Azad, who was born through IVF. After 15 years of marriage, in July 2021, Aamir and Kiran announced their divorce.

stories.title: Classmate kills medical student over one-sided love:Accused brings knife in bag; nurse injured while trying to save her
stories.summary: A 20-year-old female student studying at Pilibhit Medical College was stabbed to death by her classmate. After the incident, the accused tried to escape, but the medical college's security guards caught him on the spot and handed him over to the police. According to the police, the incident took place around 9:30 AM in the CT scan room of the medical college. The student, a resident of Bareilly, was in the CT scan room. Just then, a fellow student arrived there. An argument ensued between the two, after which the student pulled out a knife from his bag and repeatedly attacked the female student. The student ran to escape, but the accused chased her and inflicted several blows. A female employee was also injured while intervening. The condition of the student and the employee was deteriorating. Therefore, they were referred to SRMS Hospital (Shri Ram Murti Smarak Institute of Medical Sciences) in Bareilly. Around 2 PM, the student succumbed to her injuries during treatment. Initial investigation revealed that the accused was in one-sided love. Police are interrogating the accused. Meanwhile, paramedical students have gathered in protest after the murder of the student. The student's parents reached the Bareilly post-mortem house. The mother appeared distraught. People were seen comforting her. Now know the full case in detail Accused is a resident of Kanpur According to the police, Kashish Patel (20), a resident of Bareilly, was a CT scan student at Pilibhit Medical College. She arrived at the college around 9 AM on Tuesday morning. She was working with a female employee in the CT scan room. Just then, Sagar Singh (19), a resident of Kanpur who studied with Kashish, also arrived. Sagar is an X-ray technical student. According to fellow students, Kashish and Sagar were in a relationship. They had an argument over something in the morning. Brought a 12-inch knife hidden in his bag According to eyewitnesses, the accused had come prepared for the attack. He had hidden a knife about 12 inches long in his bag. He took out the knife from his bag and attacked Kashish with it right in the CT scan room. Seeing this, female employee Nidhi ran to intervene, but Sagar also attacked her. She was seriously injured by the knife in her hand. The hospital administration admitted both of them and, after primary treatment, referred them to Bareilly. There, Kashish died around 2 PM during treatment. Accused caught before he could escape After committing the crime, the accused student Sagar was trying to escape from the spot, but the security personnel of the medical college showed alertness and caught him on the spot and handed him over to the police. After this, the police have taken the accused into custody and started interrogation. Father said - The accused came to the village about 15-20 days ago In Bareilly, Kashish's father, Rohtas, is a driver. He said that he received information in the morning that a boy named Sagar had attacked his daughter with a knife, and was later caught. He said, "My daughter was pursuing a paramedical course in Pilibhit, and that boy also studied there. He had also come to their village, Kesarpur, about 15-20 days ago. When they reached Pilibhit District Hospital, their daughter's condition was serious. Later, she died." Police investigating rivalry and other aspects SP Sukirti Madhav Mishra said - The student, who was injured in an attack by a paramedical student, died during treatment at a Bareilly hospital. The accused is being interrogated to ascertain the reasons for the murder. Police are now investigating the relationship between the two students, the cause of the dispute, and the circumstances leading up to the incident. CO City Amarnath Verma said that a murder case has been registered against the accused. Police are thoroughly investigating all possible aspects, including rivalry, to present strong evidence against the accused in court. -
