stories.title: Woman's body recovered from a canal near in-laws' home:Married 5 months ago through matrimonial site in Lucknow; sister attempts suicide at police station
stories.summary: The body of a 26-year-old woman, who went missing just five months after her marriage in Lucknow, has been found in a canal around 70 km from her in-laws' home. Her parents alleged that on July 11, their daughter sent a WhatsApp voice message saying, ‘Please take me away from here by 7 am.’ When they reached her in-laws' house the following morning, they found it locked. Her phone, along with those of all her in-laws, had been switched off. Since then, the family had been sitting at Itaunja Police Station seeking action. Meanwhile, on July 13, an unidentified woman's body was recovered from the Salempur Achaka Regulator on the Indira Canal in the Nagaram area. The body remained unidentified until July 16, when the family staged a protest outside the police station. Police then sent the victim's father to the mortuary, where he identified the body as that of his daughter, Himanshi Kashyap. On learning of the identification, Himanshi's mother collapsed at the police station, while her younger sister allegedly attempted self-immolation by pouring diesel on herself. The family accused Himanshi's in-laws of murdering her and alleged that police had failed to act. Himanshi, daughter of Pawan Kashyap from Sitapur, had married Pradeep Gaur of Itaunja five months ago after the match was arranged through a matrimonial website. See 3 pictures- Family accuses police of concealing body's recovery Around 3 pm on Thursday, Himanshi's relatives staged a protest outside Itaunja Police Station, alleging that police had concealed information about the recovery of her body. During the protest, her younger sister, Kirti Kashyap, allegedly attempted self-immolation by pouring petrol on herself. Her brother, Shivraj Kashyap, claimed the family had been waiting at the police station for five days, but officers never informed them that an unidentified woman's body had already been recovered. He alleged that only after the family intensified its protest did police send their father, Pawan Kumar Kashyap, to the mortuary, where he identified Himanshi's body. Newlywed had been missing since July 12 Himanshi Kashyap married Pradeep Gaur, a resident of Turki Mohalla in Itaunja, on February 13. She was originally from Machhli Mandi in Sitapur. According to her family, around midnight on July 12, Himanshi sent a WhatsApp voice message to her younger sister asking her parents to collect her by 7 am. The family alleged that a day earlier, Himanshi had complained to her husband about being assaulted and harassed by her in-laws. When her parents arrived at her matrimonial home on July 12 to take her back, they found the house locked. The phones of Himanshi and all her in-laws were switched off. The family immediately informed police and lodged a complaint. Police awaiting post-mortem report Deputy Commissioner of Police (North) Gopal Krishna Chaudhary said that the preliminary investigation indicated the body recovered from the canal was that of Himanshi Kashyap. He said the family had formally identified the body and that further legal action would be taken after the post-mortem report is received. Father says harassment began within days of marriage Himanshi's father, Pawan Kashyap, runs a tea and samosa stall near Sitapur District Hospital. Speaking earlier at Itaunja Police Station, he said Himanshi was the second of his four children and that her marriage had been arranged through a matrimonial website. He alleged that although the family had spent beyond its means on the wedding, the groom's family continued to demand dowry. According to him, harassment began just 15 days after the marriage. The dispute had previously reached the police station, where a compromise was reached after the in-laws admitted their mistake and assured the family they would treat Himanshi well. Pawan Kashyap now alleges that those assurances were broken and his daughter was killed. He further claimed that CCTV footage from the house captured the victim's brother-in-law, Sandeep Gaur, running towards Himanshi's room carrying a trowel. According to him, the camera stopped recording shortly afterwards. Overcome with emotion while recounting the events, the father broke down and was unable to continue speaking.

stories.title: How to get the cheapest home loan?:Increase eligibility even with low salary; know hidden bank agreement charges
stories.summary: If you're planning to buy a new home and apply for a home loan, careful planning can help you secure a higher loan amount at a lower interest rate, while also saving lakhs of rupees over the loan tenure. Here are the key points every homebuyer should know. Government banks offer the lowest home loan rates Public sector banks are currently offering some of the lowest home loan interest rates. These rates are generally available only to borrowers with a CIBIL score of 750 or above. Banks may charge higher interest rates depending on an applicant's credit profile. How to increase home loan eligibility with a low salary Banks calculate your repayment capacity using the Fixed Obligation to Income Ratio (FOIR). In most cases, they allow 40–50% of your monthly income to be used for EMI payments. For example, if your monthly take-home salary is ₹30,000, the bank may allow an EMI of around ₹15,000. At an interest rate of 7.25% for a 20-year tenure, you may be eligible for a home loan of approximately ₹18.5–19 lakh. If your salary is limiting your loan eligibility, you can improve your chances by: Floating vs Fixed Interest rate: Which is better? More than 95% of home loans in 2026 are being offered at floating interest rates. A floating rate changes according to market conditions and the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) repo rate. A fixed-rate loan remains unchanged throughout the loan period but is usually 1.5% to 3% more expensive than a floating-rate loan. Some fixed-rate loans may also include prepayment penalties. When should you transfer an existing home loan? A home loan balance transfer becomes worthwhile if another bank offers an interest rate at least 1.25 percentage points lower than your current lender. For example, if your existing loan carries an 8.50% interest rate and another bank offers 7.25%, you may consider switching. Experts say a balance transfer is most beneficial within the first five to seven years of the loan, after carefully comparing processing fees, legal charges and other transfer costs. Benefits for first-time homebuyers Eligible first-time buyers may receive an interest subsidy under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY). Tax benefits are also available under the old tax regime: These tax benefits are available only to taxpayers who opt for the old tax regime. Simple ways to reduce your EMI If your EMI feels too high, consider making partial prepayments using bonuses, arrears or any additional income. This reduces the outstanding principal and can either lower your EMI or shorten the loan tenure. If your bank has reduced interest rates for new borrowers, you may also be able to switch your existing loan to the lower rate by paying a switching fee of around 0.25% to 0.50%, reducing your EMI or total interest cost. Check these hidden charges before signing the loan agreement Do not choose a home loan based only on the interest rate. Banks may also charge: Before signing the loan agreement, carefully review all applicable charges to understand the total cost of borrowing.

stories.title: Bulldozers to raze 2 mosques at Jauhar University:Azam Khan says, 'Don't know who built them'; staff claims students no longer visit
stories.summary: 38 of the 40 buildings at former Uttar Pradesh minister and Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan's Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University have been declared unauthorised. The Rampur Development Authority (RDA) has given the university 15 days to remove the structures before initiating demolition. During the process, it also emerged that two mosques inside the campus have been declared unauthorised and are also liable for demolition. Sources associated with the Rampur administration said that during the investigation, the Jauhar Ali Trust was asked about the construction of the mosques. In response, Azam Khan reportedly said, "I do not know who built these mosques." Following Rampur District Magistrate Ajay Kumar Dwivedi's demolition order, only a handful of students reached the university on July 16. By around 3 pm, the campus had fallen silent. Azam Khan's wife, Dr Tanzeen Fatima, arrived at the university at around 2 pm. After finding police personnel deployed inside the premises, she objected and had them removed. Read the full report... 'Faculty and students offer prayers here' The Rampur administration is also investigating the source of funds used to construct various buildings within Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. Two mosques have been built on the campus. One is Umar Mosque, located opposite the Department of Islamic Studies and spread across a large area. The second mosque is situated near the Administrative Block and is visible from a distance. The Rampur Development Authority says permission was never obtained to construct either mosque. In 2019, the Jauhar Ali Trust was asked how the two mosques had been built without approval and where the money for their construction had come from. According to officials, Azam Khan replied that people had come, built the mosques and left. He said faculty members and students now offered prayers there, but the trust did not know who financed or built the structures. With that statement, Azam Khan distanced himself from the construction of the mosques. However, the investigation into the funding used for their construction is still underway. Student numbers fell sharply after Azam Khan's imprisonment Our team visited the university campus. Whether it was discipline or fear of Azam Khan's family, neither students nor faculty members were willing to speak on camera. However, one faculty member, speaking off the record, said there was a time when the university had more than 5,000 students. After Azam Khan was sent to jail, enrolment reportedly dropped to around 1,000-1,200 students. The faculty member added that attendance has fallen even further since the administration issued the demolition order. Student urges government to strengthen the university We spoke to student Sidrul Nisha, who has completed her BSc and returned to seek admission to the MSc Agriculture programme. Asked how she felt about the demolition order for 38 buildings, she said the university had always provided a positive academic environment and a high standard of education. She said Azam Khan had established a good institution that enabled girls to pursue higher education and bring recognition to the district. She described the demolition action as unfair and urged the government to introduce new academic courses and strengthen the university's faculty instead. DM Ajay Kumar Dwivedi explains the demolition order Rampur District Magistrate Ajay Kumar Dwivedi answered questions regarding the notice issued to the university and the action proposed by the authorities. The notice period for Jauhar University has ended. What action will be taken? The university is located in Singan Kheda village, which falls under the jurisdiction of the Rampur Development Authority. A total of 40 buildings have been constructed. Only two have approved building plans, while the remaining 38 were built without permission. Notices were issued to the university. It has submitted a written reply and was also given an opportunity for a personal hearing. It is being claimed that the university was not under the RDA's jurisdiction when it was built. The area has come under the RDA's jurisdiction since 2024. Before that, it was under the Zila Panchayat. The university obtained approval for two buildings from the Zila Panchayat, which clearly shows it was aware of the legal requirements. However, no approval was obtained for the remaining 38 buildings. When will the demolition take place? Under the rules, the institution is given 15 days after the order is issued to remove the unauthorised structures on its own. If this is not done, the Rampur Development Authority will carry out the demolition. 'This is a public road' board installed outside university gate On July 16, the administration installed a signboard directly outside the university entrance stating, "This is a public road." A police team was also deployed near the board. However, a large gate on the road leading into the university remains locked, with Azam Khan's security guards stationed there. No one is allowed to enter the campus without their permission. According to the Public Works Department (PWD), the road passing through the university was built using government funds and is public property. Therefore, the university cannot legally block access to it. Despite the new signboard, another large gate at the far end of the nearly 2-km-long road remains permanently locked. Unless that gate is removed, the road will continue to remain blocked. There had been speculation that the administration would break open the gate on July 16, but no bulldozer was sent. Tanzeen Fatima: 'We have nothing to say at the moment' After receiving information about the police deployment, Dr Tanzeen Fatima arrived at the university on July 16. She asked the police officers at the entrance under whose orders they had come to the university. When they replied that they were acting on directions from senior officials, she responded by asking them to produce an order issued by the university rather than the police. The officers remained silent, after which she asked them to leave the premises. Later, when approached by reporters, Tanzeen Fatima said, “Everyone knows what is happening. We still have 15 days.” Asked whether the university would move the court against the demolition order, she replied, “We cannot say anything at this stage.”

stories.title: Ram Mandir donation theft accused Karunesh was alcoholic:Villagers say he had two marriages and bathed repeatedly after being touched; 'Our village is defamed'
stories.summary: "This is a village of Brahmins. Every household worships Lord Ram, and nothing like this has ever happened before. Overnight, our village has been disgraced. People now call it the 'village of the donation thief.' It has become difficult to walk with our heads held high." Residents of Jayrajpur village, located about 50 km from the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, say this with visible embarrassment. The village is home to Karunesh Pandey, one of the accused in the Ram Mandir donation theft case. Ayodhya Police have recovered ₹18 lakh from Karunesh, claiming the money was siphoned from the temple's donation boxes over time. The Special Investigation Team (SIT) also questioned his father and seized several documents from the family home. Villagers describe Karunesh as an alcoholic whose troubled personal life included two failed marriages and frequent domestic violence. They say his father had been living in Ayodhya to avoid constant family disputes. Villagers say lifestyle never reflected the alleged theft Karunesh belongs to Vashistha Ka Purwa in Jayrajpur village, where nearly 90% of the population belongs to the Brahmin community. When Dainik Bhaskar visited a tea stall near Bariyarpur crossroads, residents were discussing the temple theft. One villager said the family kept to themselves and rarely interacted with others. "His father, Ramdas, works at Khadi Village Industries in Ayodhya and lives there. He used to visit the village only on weekends. Karunesh and his elder brother had earlier worked in Surat." Another resident said the alleged theft had deeply hurt the village's reputation. "This was not an ordinary theft. It was a betrayal of people's faith. No one here is even willing to fight his legal case now because the entire village has been defamed." Despite the alleged theft involving lakhs of rupees, locals said there was no visible change in Karunesh's lifestyle or spending habits. Alcohol addiction, failed marriages and domestic violence Finding Karunesh's house was not easy, as villagers initially hesitated to identify it. Eventually, a local youth led the team there and shared details about his personal life. According to villagers, Karunesh married for the first time about ten years ago. The marriage lasted only three to four years before his wife left him, allegedly because of repeated physical abuse. After she filed a police complaint, Karunesh reportedly paid money as part of a settlement. The couple has a daughter who continues to live in the village. He remarried about five years ago, but villagers claim his behaviour remained unchanged. They allege he frequently consumed excessive alcohol, often passing out in public. Villagers would carry him home. Residents also accused him of regularly assaulting his second wife. "If she cried after being beaten, he would hit her even more and tell her not to let the neighbours hear," one villager claimed. According to locals, his drinking worsened after he started working at the Ram Mandir. Villagers describe him as eccentric A woman from the village described Karunesh as unusually obsessive about cleanliness. "He would wash his motorcycle four or five times a day. Sometimes he even washed his mobile phone. If someone accidentally touched him, he would bathe repeatedly." She said villagers often asked his wife whether he suffered from any medical condition, but she would deny it. Karunesh's elder brothers are locally known by the nicknames Fussan and Mundru. Villagers said Fussan had been working in Surat and later helped Karunesh get a job there. However, Karunesh returned to the village after working for about a year and a half. His father later arranged a job for him through a security agency in Ayodhya. Security agency job led him to the Ram Mandir While working with a security agency in Ayodhya, Karunesh came in contact with another agency—Sainik Security Services Pvt Ltd, based in Varanasi—which supplies security personnel to the Ram Mandir. About a year ago, he was posted at the temple. His responsibility was to transport donation boxes from the temple premises to the counting centre. During this assignment, he became acquainted with Anukalp Mishra, who was responsible for supervising the counting of donations. As both belonged to the same region, they developed a close association. Investigators believe the two later conspired to steal cash from the temple donations. Father says matter is before the court Karunesh's father, Ramdas, has avoided speaking to the media after the arrests. "The matter is before the court now, and the court will decide. We had no idea he had Rs 18 lakh," he said. He also claimed that Karunesh never spent lavishly. “He never even bought biscuits or chocolates for his own children. He never spoke about buying land or jewellery. We are simply maintaining the ancestral property that already belongs to the family.” Police freeze wife's bank account Police said a portion of the recovered Rs 18 lakh had been deposited in Karunesh's wife's bank account, which has now been frozen. When police took Karunesh, Lavkush and Anukalp into custody again on July 8, jewellery was recovered from Anukalp's residence, while Rs 20,000 was reportedly recovered from Karunesh's house. Investigators are still trying to determine whether the accused had plans to invest or hide the stolen money elsewhere. Officials say more details are expected to emerge after the SIT submits its final report.

stories.title: Rain alert in all 75 UP districts:Rivers in spate, rainfall 27% below normal; 2-storey house collapses in Greater Noida
stories.summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh, with thunderstorms and strong winds likely across the state. Monsoon activity has picked up once again, and cloudy skies were seen over Lucknow and nearby districts on Friday morning. Despite the recent rainfall, Uttar Pradesh has received 27% less rainfall than normal since June 1. Rivers swell as rain continues in hill states Continuous rainfall in the Himalayan region has caused the water levels of several rivers in Uttar Pradesh to rise. In Ballia, erosion has started along the banks of the Ghaghara River. In the Bansdih area, residents have begun demolishing their own permanent houses and relocating to safer places. Around 150 families have already left their homes. In Varanasi, rising water levels in the Ganga River have submerged the steps of the Dashashwamedh Ghat. However, the river is still 11.90 metres below the danger mark. In Mathura, the Yamuna River is in spate and flowing 1.30 metres below the warning level. The steps of Keshi Ghat in Vrindavan have also been submerged. In Prayagraj, water from the Ganga and Yamuna has reached shops built along the ghats. See 4 pictures- Rainfall still 27% below normal According to the weather department, Uttar Pradesh has recorded 27% below-normal rainfall so far this monsoon season. During the past 24 hours, 25 cities received rainfall, with Lakhimpur Kheri recording the highest rainfall at 22.5 mm. Rain-related incidents across the state Heavy rain and strong winds caused several incidents across Uttar Pradesh on Thursday. Two-storey house collapses in Greater Noida A two-storey house collapsed in Tilpata village of Greater Noida at around 1:30 pm on Thursday. The house was located beside a drain, and its foundation reportedly weakened due to continuous rainfall. Fortunately, no casualties were reported. Monsoon expected to become more active Senior meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh from Lucknow said a weather system is currently active over eastern Uttar Pradesh, while the monsoon trough is passing through the Terai region. He said cloud cover is present across the state, but widespread rainfall has not yet occurred. Meanwhile, the low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal is strengthening and is expected to move northwest over the next 48 hours. According to the IMD, the monsoon is expected to become more active across Uttar Pradesh after July 17, bringing more widespread and heavier rainfall.

RLP and RLD achieved one hundred percent attendance for all thirty-one sittings. BJP and Congress, the largest parties, recorded lower average attendance figures. In Rajya Sabha, regional parties also led in parliamentary attendance percentages. This analysis highlights attendance trends among various political parties in both Houses.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Aristotle: "The ideal man bears the accidents of life with dignity and…" - a powerful lesson on resilience, character and how people respond when life does not go according to plan
stories.summary: Life's unpredictable events require a dignified and graceful response from individuals. Aristotle's philosophy emphasizes maintaining composure during both good and bad fortune. Dignity involves retaining self-worth while experiencing emotions like grief or fear. Grace means responding firmly to injustice without succumbing to anger. This approach focuses on how one handles setbacks, not on avoiding them.

stories.title: Thrown into battle in two weeks': Russia plans 500,000-strong mobilisation, Ukraine claims
'Rise in instability in Iran': Indian embassy sounds alarm; urges people to leave, postpone travel
Iran's unseen Supreme Leader may turn to Putin as first foreign contact amid war
Pay quarterly, not yearly: Saudi Arabia introduces 3-month residency permit renewal option for domestic workers
Scientists studied found flies rebuild their biological clock into a separate seasonal mode
stories.summary: In a fascinating discovery, scientists have found that fruit flies adapt their internal biological clocks to survive winter by employing a genetic mechanism known as the winter lock. This adaptation allows them to remain inactive until warmer weather arrives, showcasing a seasonal shift in their molecular structure. These insights not only open avenues for innovative pest control strategies but also enhance our understanding of seasonal variations in human health issues.

stories.title: ‘People’s safety our highest priority’: Assam govt requests Army, Air Force to remain on standby for flood evacuations
'Stay here for the night': CJP's Abhijeet Dipke calls for night-long vigil ahead of 'Chalo Sansad' march
Mediterranean seagrass survives in dim seabed light by expanding its photosynthetic antenna
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered how the Mediterranean seagrass Posidonia oceanicahas adapted its photosynthetic system to survive in the dim, blue-green light of the seabed. The plant captures more light while moving energy more efficiently by altering its photosynthetic machinery. Researchers say the findings could help develop crop plants that make better use of limited sunlight under dense canopies.

stories.title: 'Not in Iran': Israeli source says supreme leader absent as internal power struggle deepens
'We intend to work with PM Modi': Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar announces entry into NDA with 20 Mamata rebels
stories.summary: Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar announced her group's move to join the ruling NDA in Parliament. Twenty former TMC MPs are now aligning with the NCPI parliamentary group. This group intends to work with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. They will support the government's initiatives and focus on constructive debate. The rebels' realignment follows the TMC's recent election defeat in West Bengal.

stories.title: Residents kept reporting Dolphins. Underwater microphones revealed their visits
stories.summary: Scientists from Kyoto University used underwater microphones to monitor dolphins in two bays along Japan's Sea of Japan coast. They found dolphin sounds only about once every 10 days, suggesting the animals visit these waters occasionally. The study also shows that long-term underwater listening can help scientists better understand and conserve marine life.

stories.title: Warming seas are bringing octopus, red mullet and bream into UK waters
stories.summary: As the seas warm, British waters are now seeing an influx of Mediterranean species. This environmental transformation is compelling local fishers to modify their traditional techniques. Notably, octopus populations are surging, impacting native shellfish and depleting other seafood supplies. In response, chefs are creatively revamping menus to highlight these new arrivals like octopus and bream, balancing the challenges with exciting culinary possibilities.

stories.title: ‘Security hole’ enabled US-Israel bombing of Ayatollah’s residence: Iran minister Araghchi
stories.summary: Iranian foreign minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi alleged a security breach allowed foreign powers access. This breach reportedly provided intelligence and influenced decision-making during a conflict. He stated attackers knew Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's routine and targeted his residence precisely. A regional leader had warned Iran about leadership being targeted before the conflict began. Araghchi noted the foreign ministry remained operational throughout the intense 40-day war.

stories.title: 'No bribes, no threats': Iran FM says US cannot scare people who expect death at any moment
Travelling to UAE? Check your flight as Kuwait, Saudi routes face disruptions
Florida is planting 15,000 milkweeds along highways to help monarch butterflies
stories.summary: Scientists and transport officials in Florida have planted 15,000 milkweed plants along roadsides to help monarch butterflies survive and reproduce. Milkweed is the only plant on which monarchs lay their eggs, making it essential for their life cycle. The project also supports bees and other pollinators while testing whether roadside habitats can become long-term wildlife corridors across the state.

stories.title: 'That's what Lindsey wanted': Trump seeks Iran's inclusion in Russia sanctions bill
stories.summary: President Trump wants Republican lawmakers to add Iran to the Russia sanctions bill. This legislation targets major buyers of Russian energy and aims to hold them accountable. The revised bill refines tariff authority and adds new measures for sanctions evasion. It also incorporates acts targeting Chinese support for Russia's defense industry. The updated legislation seeks to prevent Tehran from acquiring nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia records 22.5% rise in Umrah arrivals as over 1.27 million pilgrims visit kingdom
Elisha Cuthbert has sold her longtime LA home for $1.93 million after cutting the asking price
stories.summary: Hollywood actress Elisha Cuthbert has sold her Los Angeles home for $1.93 million after several unsuccessful attempts to find a buyer. The property was sold shortly after a final price cut. The sale comes as Cuthbert returns to acting following a four-year break, during which she focused on raising her two children with husband Dion Phaneuf.

stories.title: 'No permission sought or granted': Delhi Police on CJP's Parliament march
stories.summary: Delhi Police has denied permission for a proposed march to Parliament on July 20. Prohibitory orders are in effect across the New Delhi district, banning assemblies. Unauthorized gatherings will face legal action under new Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita provisions. The Delhi High Court previously upheld the Centre's intervention in Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike. Authorities urge public cooperation to ensure security during the upcoming Parliament session.

stories.title: Scientists discover a ‘third cell’ that helps regrow hair
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking development, Japanese researchers have unveiled a pivotal third cell integral to the regeneration of hair follicles. This finding holds the potential to reverse conditions like baldness and thinning hair by collaborating with two established cell types. Successful experiments conducted on mice demonstrated the complete cycle of hair growth, paving the way for pioneering regenerative treatments aimed at combating hair loss.

stories.title: US envoy rejects Mamdani's threat to arrest Netanyahu during NYC visit
'Parliament should discuss if new anti-defection law needed': Congress' Manish Tewari after TMC, Shiv Sena (UBT) splits
stories.summary: Congress MP Manish Tewari advocates for a new anti-defection law. He believes the Lok Sabha composition no longer reflects the 2024 voter mandate. Recent party splits have weakened Indian democracy and opportunistic politics are prevalent. TMC and Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs have switched allegiance to the ruling NDA. Tewari stresses the need to address these developments during the upcoming Parliament session.

stories.title: The real-life Gilmore Girls house from the pilot episode is for sale for $2.7 million in Ontario, where Unionville first stood in for Stars Hollow
stories.summary: A historic Unionville home, which served as Lorelai and Rory Gilmore’s house in the pilot episode, is now for sale. This property, listed at $3.88 million CAD, offers a tangible connection to the beloved show. The surrounding neighborhood also featured as key Stars Hollow locations, enhancing its appeal. The house, built around 1875, blends Victorian charm with modern amenities for comfortable living.

stories.title: Iran's shadow fleet rushed $6 billion of oil to China during brief US truce: Report
'He intends to continue the fast': Sonam Wangchuk's wife vows to lead Parliament march
stories.summary: Gitanjali J Angmo will lead a march to Parliament representing her husband, Sonam Wangchuk. Wangchuk continues his indefinite hunger strike from Safdarjung Hospital after being moved there. The Delhi High Court declined to order his immediate transfer to a private facility. Angmo urged protesters to maintain peace and remain vigilant against disruptions. Security has been heightened across New Delhi ahead of the planned march.

stories.title: DNA from 457 koalas suggests the species nearly went extinct 100,000 years ago, before humans...
stories.summary: Approximately 100,000 years ago, koalas faced near extinction due to brutal ice ages. A recent genetic study triumphantly highlights that this crisis occurred well before humans populated Australia. By examining koala genomes, scientists have beautifully illustrated how climate shifts triggered significant declines in their population. Presently, however, modern threats stem largely from human activities, underscoring the urgent need for dedicated conservation measures.

stories.title: 'Avoid cloak-and-dagger tactics': Derek O'Brien writes to PM Modi on delimitation bill, seeks all-party meet
stories.summary: Trinamool Congress leader Derek O'Brien urged Prime Minister Modi to convene an all-party meeting. He expressed concerns over proposed delimitation legislation and the Foreign Contribution Amendment bill. O'Brien described these measures as 'draconian' and 'cowboy legislation' in his letter. The opposition fears the delimitation exercise could reduce southern states' parliamentary representation. The Foreign Contribution Amendment bill may tighten government oversight of charitable organizations.

stories.title: ‘No state has witnessed such a political change since Independence’: Amit Shah on Bengal
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah called West Bengal's political change unprecedented since Independence. He criticized the previous Left Front and Trinamool Congress governments. Shah attended the foundation stone laying for a new dairy project. This project aims to boost the state's dairy sector and farmer incomes. The minister concluded his three-day visit to West Bengal.

stories.title: After 38 years, DNA test reveals two US men were switched at birth; families sue North Dakota hospital
Archaeologists unearthed a rare 2,600-year-old Assyrian stele, a decade after ISIS damaged the city
stories.summary: A stunning 2,600-year-old Assyrian monument has surfaced in Nineveh, Iraq, celebrating the architectural feats of King Ashurbanipal. Unearthed amidst restoration efforts at the Shamash Gate, this stone artifact reveals essential details about Assyrian urban development. This significant find stands as a testament to the resilience of cultural identities, aiding in reconciling historical disruptions and preservation.

stories.title: 'NCPI recognised by EC': Sudip Bandyopadhyay hits back after opposition's walkout over TMC rebels' presence
stories.summary: The Nationalist Citizens Party of India attended an all-party meeting ahead of the Monsoon Session. Opposition parties staged a symbolic walkout to protest the invitation extended to NCPI leaders. NCPI leaders defended their party's recognition by the Election Commission and its MPs' presence. They stated that the Lok Sabha Speaker would clarify seating arrangements and disqualification matters. The government defended inviting the NCPI as they had requested recognition.

stories.title: Evening newswrap: HC rejects wife's plea to move Sonam Wangchuk to private hospital; Spain's largest wildfire burns 16,000 hectares, and more
Scientists identify rare meteorite behind dinosaur extinction
stories.summary: Scientists have identified a rare CO chondrite meteorite as the impactor that caused dinosaur extinction. This space rock, which struck Earth 66 million years ago, wiped out most life. Advanced nickel isotope analysis traced the meteorite's chemical signature to the deadly impact event. The rare nature of this projectile highlights the dinosaurs' extreme misfortune. This impact created the Chicxulub crater and led to a mass extinction.

stories.title: Who will care for the child? Why many women remain outside the workforce
'Govt was within its right': Why Delhi HC backed Sonam Wangchuk's hospital shift
stories.summary: The Delhi high court rejected a plea to move Sonam Wangchuk to a private hospital. The court noted no force was used in his transfer to Safdarjung Hospital. Family members have been granted round-the-clock access to the fasting activist. Doctors are monitoring his health and administering oral substances with consent. The government acted within its rights to provide care for Wangchuk.

stories.title: Tiny plastics in drinking water may help harmful bacteria resist disinfectants
stories.summary: New research reveals nanoplastics can strengthen harmful bacterial biofilms in water systems. These tiny plastic particles help microbes survive disinfection treatments more effectively. This makes maintaining clean drinking water infrastructure significantly more challenging. The presence of nanoplastics may contribute to the rise of antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Understanding these interactions is crucial for public health and water management efforts.

stories.title: ‘Dialogue, not silence’: Naveen Patnaik urges dialogue with students protesting exam crisis
'Big mistake': CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke accuses Delhi Police of 'kidnapping' Sonam Wangchuk
stories.summary: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk was removed from the Jantar Mantar protest site. He had been on an indefinite hunger strike for over twenty days. Authorities moved him to Safdarjung Hospital for necessary medical monitoring. Protesters and the Cockroach Janta Party criticized this forceful removal. However, the Delhi High Court later upheld the government's decision.

stories.title: Flash floods rip through Jammu and Kashmir as rain fury leaves trail of destruction - watch
No relief for Wangchuk: Delhi HC backs government's move to shift Sonam to hospital, says no force used
stories.summary: The Delhi HC upheld the Centre's decision to move Sonam Wangchuk to Safdarjung Hospital. The court found the government's action was not arbitrary given his health condition. His wife's petition for transfer to a private hospital was declined by the court. The court noted Wangchuk's family has been given unrestricted access to him.

stories.title: Canadian lawyer faces 6-month suspension for citing ChatGPT cases in court hearing
Calcutta HC halts demolition of Abhishek Banerjee's Amtala office
stories.summary: The Calcutta High Court has ordered a halt to demolition work at Abhishek Banerjee's office. This directive came after an anti-encroachment drive was initiated at the premises. The Trinamool Congress leader had alleged political motivation behind the demolition efforts. He stated the office was built legally on purchased land with permissions. The district administration claimed the structure violated building plan rules.

stories.title: 16,000 hectares burned, over 1,100 evacuated: Spain's largest wildfire rages on
Rajya Sabha MPs' salaries, perks cost exchequer Rs 262 crore in two years
stories.summary: The RTI response showed that expenditure on sitting Rajya Sabha members rose sharply from more than Rs 98 crore in 2024-25 to over Rs 163 crore in 2025-26, marking an increase of nearly Rs 65 crore in a year. The expenditure covered salaries, domestic and international travel, office expenses, medical reimbursements and other facilities provided to MPs.

stories.title: Doctors' assault: Maharashtra IMA suspends July 20 strike after HC stays Shiv Sena corporator's bail
Astronomers just spotted erythrulose, the tastiest sugar found in some berries here on Earth, and why this discovery could change how we search for life in space
Earth has regulated its climate for 60 million years through a hidden ocean feedback
stories.summary: A new study has identified a natural process that may have helped keep Earth's climate stable for the past 60 million years. Researchers found that changes in sea level controlled the amount of phosphate reaching the oceans, affecting marine life, carbon burial beneath the seafloor and the level of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere. The findings offer a new explanation for how Earth naturally regulated long-term warming and cooling.

stories.title: 'In favour of the Women's Reservation Bill but...': DMK presses Centre on delimitation
'NCPI requested recognition, how can you ignore?' Kiren Rijiju after opposition walkout over TMC rebels invitation
stories.summary: Union minister Kiren Rijiju defended inviting the Nationalist Citizens Party of India to an all-party meeting. Opposition parties staged a symbolic walkout protesting the invitation to rebel Trinamool Congress MPs. Rijiju stated the government followed parliamentary norms and could not ignore the party's recognition request. Eight bills are listed for the upcoming Monsoon Session, which begins Monday. All parties have the right to express views and cooperate for the nation.

stories.title: Sable Island is a remote sand island with no permanent residents, yet hundreds of wild horses roam freely across its shifting dunes
Scientists use teeth to trace childhood journeys of Africans freed from slave ships
stories.summary: A new study has uncovered the childhood origins of 152 Africans rescued from illegal slave ships and taken to Saint Helena nearly 200 years ago. Using tooth chemistry, ancient DNA and historical records, researchers found they came from different parts of Central Africa, with many forced to travel long distances before reaching the coast. The findings help restore the identities of people whose lives were erased by the transatlantic slave trade.

stories.title: 'Equal rights for Ram, Rahim, Ravinder and Robin': CM Mohan Yadav after Madhya Pradesh cabinet approves UCC
stories.summary: Announcing the approval, the chief minister said the proposed legislation was aimed at guaranteeing equal rights for every citizen, irrespective of religion, and congratulated his Cabinet colleagues for unanimously backing the Bill. "Today, the Madhya Pradesh Cabinet has wholeheartedly and unanimously approved the Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026. I wish to extend my congratulations to my esteemed Cabinet colleagues and to all of you," he said.

stories.title: New bills, old battles, changed equations: What awaits Parliament this Monsoon Session
stories.summary: Parliament's Monsoon Session begins Monday with a packed legislative agenda. The government aims to pass the Women's Reservation Bill after its earlier defeat. Opposition parties face electoral losses and alliance collapses, altering parliamentary arithmetic. Several key bills are listed, including the FCRA and Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan. The government hopes to secure passage with adjusted strategies and potential support.

stories.title: 'Not conducive to patient's care': Safdarjung hospital responds to Wangchuk wife's claims
Quote of the day by Warren Buffett: “Be fearful when others are greedy, and be greedy when…” - the powerful mindset behind long-term success
NIOS concludes training programme for ASHA certification, aims to certify 10 lakh workers in next phase
'Those meant to uphold law have become lawbreakers': Abhishek Banerjee slams Bengal Police after his office demolition
'Second attack in two days': Kuwait says Iran hit power, water desalination plant
'Tear gas guns arrived': CJP says BJP 'goons', Delhi Police lurking to 'create mischief'
stories.summary: In another post, the CJP posted a photo of a security personnel sitting with a tear gas gun at the protest site. Earlier, Wangchuk described the proposed July 20 Parliament march as India's "second freedom movement", calling for "freedom from fear" and "freedom from injustice" while urging supporters to make the mobilisation a "big success".

stories.title: 'Trust's account should be made public': Rahul, Kharge write to PM over alleged theft of Ram Mandir donations
Mount Olympus, the mythological home of Zeus and the ancient Greek gods, is being considered for UNESCO World Heritage status as Greece seeks protection for its tallest mountain
stories.summary: Mount Olympus, a site of myth and nature, seeks UNESCO World Heritage recognition. This ancient Greek mountain is home to gods and diverse ecosystems. Locals hope for global acknowledgment to ensure its continued protection. The nomination process involves careful review and potential further requirements. Recognition would bring responsibilities for preserving its unique cultural and natural values.

J&K: Flash floods, landslides wreak havoc in Poonch-Rajouri belt; 11 dead, several missing
Centre to hold all-party meeting today ahead of Monsoon Session; NEET, Wangchuk, Ram Mandir row on agenda
'Ensure the smooth functioning of the House': Rijiju urges parties ahead of Monsoon Session
'Your silence is unacceptable': Rahul, Kharge write to PM Modi on Ram Mandir donation theft
stories.summary: Demanding a probe into financial affairs of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, both the leaders said that the "findings and the Trust's accounts should be made public so that every devotee knows how their offerings have been utilised". ​Ahead of the Monoon Session of the Parliament, the leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, and the Rajya Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge, urged PM to "immediately order an independent and comprehensive investigation.

stories.title: Safdarjung Hospital issues Sonam Wangchuk health update; wife alleges 'illegal detention'- top developments
Overnight rain brings J&K's Rajouri to a standstill as flash floods wreak havoc
stories.summary: More than 50 families living near Abdullah Bridge were forced to leave their homes after floodwaters flooded the settlement. Another locality near Tariq Bridge was also affected, prompting police to respond to distress calls and help residents move to safer places away from the riverbanks. Rescue and relief teams, assisted by the district administration, were deployed to evacuate affected families and assess the damage.

stories.title: AIIMS expert backs urgent care for Sonam Wangchuk, activist denies
Who is WardrobeWinter? Meet Plaqueboymax’s roommate at Kai Cenat’s Streamer University 2026
stories.summary: WardrobeWinter became one of the biggest breakout creators from Kai Cenat’s Streamer University 2026. Already popular on TikTok and Twitch, he drew even more attention after his roommate clashes with Plaqueboymax. With help from counsellor YourRAGE, the two talked through their problems, agreed on simple ground rules and eventually ended the situation with a hug.

stories.title: US launches fresh airstrikes on Iran after attack on American troops in Jordan
stories.summary: United States forces launched new airstrikes against Iran on President Donald Trump's orders. These strikes aim to degrade Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping. The operation also retaliates for recent attacks on American service members in Jordan. The US Central Command confirmed the military action began at 6 p.m. ET. Iran has not yet issued any official comment on the developments.

stories.title: Using abusive language, swearing don't count as obscenity under IPC: Supreme Court
stories.summary: Supreme Court clarified that abusive language is not obscenity under law. Mere swear words and profanities do not constitute an offense. The court set aside a conviction for using abusive slurs during an altercation. Obscenity requires a lascivious element appealing to prurient interests. Such words must also cause annoyance to others in public places.

stories.title: NDA ranks boosted as Om Birla okays 6 rebel UBT MPs joining Shiv Sena
Skyroot puts first private rocket in orbit & India in elite club; Vikram-1 delivers 6 payloads after 35-minute delay
stories.summary: Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-1 rocket successfully launched into low Earth orbit on Saturday. This historic mission placed six payloads into their targeted orbit successfully. India now becomes the third nation with private orbital launch capability. The Hyderabad-based startup achieved this significant milestone on its first attempt. This launch signifies a new era for private Indian space industry operations.

stories.title: Meet Indian-origin tech leader Uday Ruddaraju, who has become OpenAI's CTO of Compute
Another House panel defers edu reforms report adoption; move seen as part of govt's outreach to oppn for delimit bill support
stories.summary: Two parliamentary committees have postponed approving their reports on significant legislation. This development occurs as the government seeks opposition support for other political proposals. The anti-graft bill and higher education regulator bills face widespread protest. Both bills may not be presented during the current parliamentary session. Congress criticizes the government's handling of these controversial legislative matters.

stories.title: Medical colleges to decide own faculty appointments, promotions: National Medical Commission
stories.summary: Medical colleges now decide faculty appointments and promotions independently. The National Medical Commission has ended routine eligibility clearances for these positions. This change aims to improve institutional accountability and reduce unnecessary referrals. Applicants dissatisfied with decisions can seek a review within thirty days. The regulator will now focus on exceptional cases involving regulatory ambiguity.

stories.title: India flags cross-border terrorism at US meet on left extremism
stories.summary: But Rubio downplays radical islamist extremism

stories.title: Quote of the day by Jimmy Carter: 'We should live our lives as though Christ were coming this afternoon'
CBSE 2nd Board results: 3 lakh students improve scores
School holiday extended in Kashmir, Amarnath yatra suspended as Met forecasts downpour
stories.summary: Kashmir school holidays have been extended by three days due to adverse weather. The Amarnath yatra is temporarily suspended from both routes as a precautionary measure. An adverse weather spell is expected from July 20 to July 23 across the region. This system may cause landslides and flash floods in vulnerable areas. Surface transport disruptions are also anticipated on major roads.

stories.title: Partial shutdown in Doda, Kishtwar over man’s death in run-in with cops
stories.summary: A 30-year-old man died after being shot by police near Bhaderwah town. Shops and businesses remained closed in Doda and Kishtwar districts on Saturday. The man allegedly tried to snatch a service rifle from a police personnel. This incident led to injuries for three special operations group personnel as well. Mobile internet services were suspended for a second consecutive day as a precaution.

stories.title: Army opens fire after observing suspicious movement along LoC In J-K’s Rajouri
Quote of the day by Boris Johnson: 'My policy on cake is pro having it and pro eating it' and how it became a key phrase of Brexit
NCB seizes 5kg heroin smuggled from Pakistan in Poonch, 1 held
stories.summary: Narcotics Control Bureau seized five kilograms of high-grade heroin in Poonch district. An alleged smuggler was arrested during a raid in Kosalyain village on Saturday. This seizure is considered one of the largest drug hauls in the border district. Investigators are working to identify the intended recipients and handlers. This incident highlights ongoing cross-border narcotics smuggling attempts.

stories.title: Mehbooba rejects Farooq’s invite to join Jantar Mantar protest; Engineer Rashid to walk barefoot in solidarity
Skyroot’s orbital launch: India’s own SpaceX is born, startup to give country another option to Isro for satellite launches
stories.summary: Skyroot Aerospace successfully launched India's first privately developed orbital-class rocket, Vikram-1. This historic flight reached low Earth orbit and deployed six payloads for various applications. The launch signifies a major step for India's private space sector and its global market aspirations. Other Indian space startups are expected to accelerate their orbital rocket programs following this success.

stories.title: Rs 70,000 cr investments proposed for def corridors in UP, TN; Rs 10,000 crore already invested: Rajnath
stories.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh highlighted India's strong defence preparedness and self-reliance. Advanced systems like Akash Teer and BrahMos were effectively used during Operation Sindoor. Defence industrial corridors in UP and Tamil Nadu are fostering indigenous manufacturing and global integration. Positive indigenisation lists and a new Defence Acquisition Procedure are accelerating domestic production. Seventy-five percent of the defence modernisation budget now supports Indian industries.

stories.title: India rolls out 'White Rabbit' tech to secure Indian Standard Time network: What it means
stories.summary: India has launched a secure, indigenous time signal network for critical infrastructure. This initiative reduces reliance on foreign timing sources for essential services. The system uses White Rabbit technology for highly accurate time synchronization. It aims to enhance reliability in banking, telecom, and power grid operations. This development supports India's technological self-reliance and digital economy.

stories.title: I was discouraged from taking bold decision to privatise space sector, today you proved me right: PM Modi to Skyroot after Vikram-1 successful launch
stories.summary: India achieved a historic milestone with the successful launch of its first private orbital rocket. Prime Minister Narendra Modi lauded the achievement, emphasizing faith in the nation's youth. This success positions India as the third country with indigenous private orbital launch capabilities. Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-1 rocket carried a special message for the universe. The event signifies a new era for India's growing private space sector.

stories.title: 'Are you comfortable with daily late evening calls?' Techie who returned to India from US shocked to see this question on online application
Quote of the day by Socrates' student Plato: "One of the penalties for refusing to participate in politics is…"
stories.summary: Plato's ancient warning highlights the consequences of political disengagement. Choosing not to participate means others will make decisions for you. Withdrawal does not exempt individuals from the outcomes of governance. Informed citizens must remain engaged to hold power accountable. This ensures that capable individuals, not just ambitious ones, shape society.

stories.title: Sister of Indian woman stabbed to death in London demands justice
Iran Supreme Leader's message to US: Mojtaba Khamenei calls Trump's signature worthless, issues new warning
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader warned the United States of "unforgettable lessons" if attacks continued. He declared President Trump's signature "worthless and invalid" amid escalating conflict. Tehran suspended commitments under a recent interim agreement, citing US breaches. Both nations exchanged strikes on military and infrastructure targets. Regional security and global energy supplies remain a concern.

stories.title: 'Entire BJP trembling with fear': Prashant Kishor on Bankipur assembly bypoll
stories.summary: Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor claims the BJP fears his electoral debut. He alleges the ruling party is now campaigning door-to-door for votes. Kishor urges voters to reject money and food distribution practices. The Jan Suraaj Party aims to offer a credible political alternative. The Bankipur bypoll is scheduled for July 30 in Bihar.

stories.title: US Air Force airman killed in heavy equipment accident at California space base
Amarnath, Vaishno Devi Yatras temporarily suspended due to bad weather
stories.summary: Authorities have temporarily suspended the Amarnath and Vaishno Devi Yatras due to inclement weather. The decision was made as a precautionary measure to ensure the safety of all pilgrims. Pilgrims are advised to remain patient and follow official communication channels for updates. The Shri Amarnathji Yatra will remain suspended from both Pahalgam and Baltal routes. The Yatra will resume once weather conditions are deemed safe for travel.

stories.title: CBSE declares Class 10 second edition board results; nearly 60% candidates improve performance
'Ayodhya verdict not fully implemented': Nirmohi Akhara moves Supreme Court, seeks reconstitution of Ram Temple trust
After paying $32000 tuition fee for 2 years, Indian students in Canada told they are not eligible for post-graduation work permit
From Article 370 to Ram-Nami, National Awards capture many ideas of India
stories.summary: Political history and military valour dominate the marquee honours, while stories of ageing, caste resistance, women’s agency and ecological renewal give the verdict its human core.

stories.title: 'Netanyahu belongs in the Hague': Mamdani considering Israel PM's arrest during NYC visit
Indian-origin woman jailed in UK for more than 2 years over Rs 2.8 crore Covid loan fraud
Round-the-clock surveillance, barricading, extra forces: Delhi Police gear up for CJP's 'Sansad chalo' march
stories.summary: Delhi Police increased surveillance and vehicle checks for an upcoming Parliament march. Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk was hospitalized after his health deteriorated during a hunger strike. The Cockroach Janta Party plans a march to Parliament on July 20. Authorities are unlikely to grant permission for the unauthorized march. Security has been heightened around Parliament and sensitive protest locations.

stories.title: 'Blood for blood': Iran displays giant billboard with Donald, Melania and Trump children in coffins
stories.summary: A new billboard in Tehran shows Donald Trump and his family above coffins draped in the US flag. The prominent slogan 'Blood for Blood' signals Iran's intent for revenge against recent strikes. This display follows other murals targeting Trump, including one showing him in an open coffin. These actions occur as military tensions between Iran and the United States intensify.

stories.title: 'Happened so fast that ... ': Protestors recount how police took away Sonam Wangchuk in 5 minutes
stories.summary: Eyewitnesses described Sonam Wangchuk's swift removal from Jantar Mantar by police. White bedsheets shielded the operation, preventing public view of the activist's departure. Police stated Wangchuk was taken to hospital following medical advice and court orders. Protesters alleged the police action was timed to minimize visibility and support. Despite the removal, demonstrators vowed to continue their protest for educational reforms.

stories.title: Big setback for Uddhav Thackeray! Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla recognises 6 UBT rebel MPs joining Shinde's Shiv Sena
'Don't wait for tragic outcome': Anna Hazare urges Centre to hold talks with Sonam Wangchuk
stories.summary: Anna Hazare urged the government to hold talks with Sonam Wangchuk. Wangchuk was hospitalized after his hunger strike entered its twenty-first day. Police removed him from Jantar Mantar amid heavy security measures. Opposition leaders condemned the government's actions and suppression of dissent. stories.summary: Kick streamer Ice Poseidon's planned India trip was cancelled after his visa was revoked. He learned his visa was denied due to his contact, Deepak, who has alleged criminal issues. Ice Poseidon presented this gathered information as his reason for denial.

stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath criticized former CM Akhilesh Yadav's tenure. He alleged Yadav lacked public engagement and a development vision for the state. Adityanath highlighted the BJP government's welfare schemes and development projects. He contrasted current progress with the previous administration's perceived failures. The chief minister also accused the opposition of betraying farmers and compromising law and order.

stories.title: Streamer University 2026 ending date explained as Kai Cenat reveals what happens before July 20
stories.summary: The grand finale of Streamer University 2026, hosted by Kai Cenat, is set for July 20th morning. Alumni have begun to flock to campus to engage with students in these last days of festivities. Kai has made it clear that any rule infractions could lead to expulsion from campus. 'Zero tolerance against terrorism not just a statement': Rajnath Singh's message to Pakistan
stories.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh stated India's zero tolerance for terrorism is a line of action. Operation Sindoor demonstrated India's retaliatory military capabilities and technological advancements. The government trusts India's defence capabilities more than previous administrations did. India's defence production has reached a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore annually. Defence exports have surged significantly, positioning India as a global security partner.

stories.title: Ludwig’s Streamer Games 2026: Event dates, livestream, venue, tickets, and creator lineup
stories.summary: Streamer Games 2026 is set to ignite the screens on August 1 and 2, hosted at the University of Southern California. Viewers can catch all the thrilling competitions live on platforms like YouTube and Twitch. With an impressive lineup of popular creators confirmed to participate, fans can find tickets and additional information on the official Streamer Games website.

stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi criticized the Centre's removal of Sonam Wangchuk from Jantar Mantar. Police shifted the climate activist to Safdarjung Hospital for medical observation and treatment. Opposition leaders condemned the Centre's actions, calling it suppression of peaceful dissent. The protest demanded resignation and reforms in the education system.

Investigators suspect crude bomb explosives caused the explosion which damaged a residential building. stories.summary: The United States is currently grappling with the most significant Cyclospora outbreak in its history, with over one thousand six hundred confirmed cases spanning forty-five states. stories.summary: Skyroot Aerospace launched India's first privately developed orbital rocket, Vikram-1. The vehicle successfully placed four technology demonstration satellites into low-Earth orbit. This launch marks a significant milestone in opening India's space sector to private companies. Vikram-1 utilized advanced carbon-composite structures and a restartable liquid-fuelled module. The mission validates India's capabilities in private orbital launch vehicle development.

stories.summary: Congress MP Manish Tewari addressed speculation regarding his interaction with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. How does a hydrogen train work?
stories.summary: Hydrogen trains are an innovative solution for clean transit, producing zero direct emissions through fuel cells that convert hydrogen into electricity. These trains can seamlessly run on existing railway lines without needing overhead power lines. India’s version operates with compressed hydrogen held at high pressure. However, hurdles remain in hydrogen production, safety, and cost-effectiveness, with successful implementation reliant on affordable green hydrogen and robust infrastructure.

stories.title: 'Historic new frontier': PM Modi hails 'talent of youth' ahead of Skyroot's maiden orbital attempt with Vikram-1 launch
stories.summary: Skyroot Aerospace prepares for the maiden orbital launch of Vikram-1 today. Prime Minister Modi hailed this as a historic new frontier for India. This staffing gap has widened significantly since 2019, impacting critical mission development. Recruitment processes were delayed due to Covid-19 and reforms, creating a substantial gap. Efforts are underway to fill over two thousand vacancies by late 2026. The department must rebuild its workforce while retaining experienced scientists.

stories.summary: A man was shot dead in Doda district following an encounter with police personnel. Mobile internet services were suspended across the district as tensions escalated rapidly. Three police officers sustained injuries during the confrontation on Jai valley road. Locals protested the death, and a shutdown was called by a local outfit. Authorities are investigating the incident, and senior officials are present in Bhaderwah.

stories.summary: A Jammu court rejected Kamal Singh Jamwal's bail plea in the Farooq Abdullah assassination attempt case. The judge cited wider implications for public order and democratic stability in the decision. Jamwal's medical plea was also dismissed, with no evidence of mental disorder presented. The outcomes of this research present an essential blueprint for focused conservation financing and the safeguarding of marine life during the alarming bleaching epidemic.

This discovery highlights the importance of historical observations and modern science.

stories.title: Meet Chelsie Anderson: American woman who accidentally became a Mexican drug cartel queen
stories.summary: Chelsie Anderson went from serving tables to becoming a pivotal figure in drug trafficking. Scientists propose enhanced land management practices to safeguard these critical ecological processes.

These leaders resigned from their previous posts last month after election results. Their return to the Upper House on BJP tickets marks a significant political shift. This development follows the Trinamool Congress's defeat in recent assembly elections.

stories.title: Scientists discover first-ever antidote to red tide toxin
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking study, researchers have identified a frog protein capable of neutralizing saxitoxin, a harmful neurotoxin. This unique protein functions as a molecular sponge, effectively binding to the toxin in the bloodstream. Experiments on mice demonstrated its ability to prevent and even reverse the effects of lethal poisoning, offering significant possibilities for combatting paralytic shellfish poisoning incidents globally.

stories.summary: PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti criticized the government's silence on Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike. Wangchuk has been on an indefinite hunger strike for twenty days demanding action. He is protesting alleged irregularities in the NEET examination and paper leaks. Doctors have warned of critical health risks if the hunger strike continues. Wangchuk vows to continue his protest until July twentieth for a government response.

This billionaire’s $300 million superyacht cruised through the Strait of Hormuz without any problems
stories.summary: Motor Yacht A, under the ownership of billionaire Andrey Melnichenko, recently traversed the Strait of Hormuz amidst increased military tensions that have prompted commercial vessels to postpone their voyages. Following the imposition of Western sanctions after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Melnichenko relocated his assets to the Gulf, particularly after his Sailing Yacht A was confiscated by Italian authorities in March 2022.

stories.title: 'Absurd': Putin critic Boris Nadezhdin found guilty in 'extremist symbols' case
stories.summary: Russian opposition politician Boris Nadezhdin was convicted of displaying extremist symbols. This ruling prevents him from contesting upcoming parliamentary elections in Russia. Nadezhdin had previously criticized President Vladimir Putin and the Ukraine war. Another Putin critic, Ilya Remeslo, was also arrested on charges of spreading false military information. Russian authorities have intensified crackdowns on dissent and free speech since 2022.

Rare Atlantic Niña and Super El Niño may suppress hurricanes, lowering US landfall risk
stories.summary: A rare Atlantic Niña is developing alongside a strong Super El Niño event. These ocean patterns may suppress hurricane formation in the Atlantic Ocean. Increased wind shear and sinking air create an atmospheric shield against storms. However, experts caution that a quieter season does not eliminate hurricane risks. Residents in vulnerable areas should continue their normal hurricane preparations.

The Bill could not pass the numbers test during the Budget session. Opposition parties, which were united in their opposition to the Bill in April, appear to be divided now over the idea of uniform seat increase. Some parties may support the bill if their concerns are addressed. The Congress fears isolation and has requested an all-party meeting for discussions. The proposed 50% seat increase aims to facilitate women's reservation without altering current proportions.

stories.title: China’s giant sinkholes are protecting an endangered tree, but they may also be trapping its future
stories.summary: In China, vast sinkholes provide a refuge for the rare Magnolia aromatica trees, buffering them against the harsh realities of climate change. These subterranean havens create stable microclimates that support these endangered species. However, this isolation can limit genetic diversity and hinder the trees' adaptability to future environmental changes. To ensure their survival, conservation efforts must focus on safeguarding habitats while facilitating gene flow between populations.

A win confirms preparation worked, while a loss creates doubt to overcome. Returning to routine after setbacks creates opportunities to move forward. This principle applies beyond sports to various life challenges and failures.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Eric Hoffer: 'In times of change, learners inherit the Earth, while the learned find themselves beautifully equipped for a world that no longer exists'

Those who are willing to learn and adapt will thrive, while others may find themselves left behind. Continuous education is now a must for both professionals and students. By embracing change and acquiring new skills, individuals unlock new opportunities. Lifelong learning promotes relevance and readiness for the challenges that lie ahead.

Less snowfall leads to warmer, smaller ponds with concentrated nutrients. Climate change projections indicate reduced snowpack, impacting these delicate ecosystems. These small water bodies play a crucial role in mountain biodiversity and nutrient cycling.

stories.title: A British island became known as the 'island of death' after a secret anthrax experiment and remained under quarantine for 48 years
Andy Burnham set to be new UK Prime Minister, takes over from Keir Starmer on Monday
US fugitive featured on 'America's Most Wanted' arrested after 20 years on the run
Indian-origin man pleads guilty to manslaughter after fatal M4 crash in West London
In 1999, archaeologists found a teenage Inca girl frozen on a 6,739-metre volcano, where she had remained untouched for more than 500 years
Man steals kitten to rob bank, but gets caught
stories.summary: A curious case unfolded when a man stole a kitten named Magnolia from a pet store, employing her as a smokescreen during a bank robbery. As he demanded money from the teller, law enforcement swiftly intervened, capturing the suspect. Officers later found Magnolia safe in the bank manager's office. This charming kitten is now ready to find a loving and responsible family to call her own.

stories.title: Ex-Badrinath temple officer Rajendra Chauhan arrested in donation theft case after SIT grilling
stories.summary: Former Badrinath temple officer Rajendra Chauhan was arrested for alleged donation theft. CCTV footage showed Chauhan collecting cash bundles and putting them into his pocket. The Special Investigation Team received an internal inquiry report from the temple committee. Investigators identified more suspects after examining fresh CCTV footage from recent dates. The investigation into the temple donation theft case is currently ongoing.

stories.title: 'Whoever kills Trump ...': Iran-backed Iraqi militia puts $10 million bounty on US president
Quote of the day by William Gibson: 'The future is already here—it's just not evenly distributed'
stories.summary: William Gibson's observation emphasizes the disparate distribution of technological advancements in today's world. Innovations often emerge in isolated areas before reaching broader audiences. Access to these developments is influenced by available resources and educational opportunities, highlighting the ongoing challenge of achieving equitable progress. As we embrace change and strive for inclusive access, we can better shape a collective future for everyone.

stories.title: 'A national cause, more discussions needed': JPC defers draft report on PM, CMs removal bill
stories.summary: A joint parliamentary committee deferred its draft report on removing leaders facing serious charges. The panel decided more consultations were needed before adopting its five recommendations. Members voted on recommendations, with some BJP members also voting against initial proposals. The committee suggested suspending, not permanently removing, leaders detained for thirty days. This bill seeks to amend the Government of Union Territories Act, 1963.

stories.title: Newborn kangaroos are born tiny, blind and embryo-like, but scientists say their arms develop early so they can crawl to the mother’s pouch and survive
China built “ghost” subway stations in empty fields before residents arrived, but years later new homes, roads and businesses began growing around them
stories.summary: China's empty subway stations were once seen as ghost cities and poor planning. However, this infrastructure development was a strategy to attract future urban growth. New roads and housing eventually surrounded these stations, transforming isolated areas. This approach involved building foundations before people arrived to stimulate development. Such ambitious projects carry significant financial burdens and potential vulnerabilities.

stories.title: 'No proof, no facts': Former envoy Sanjay Verma on Nijjar case as US indictment clears India
'Constant onslaught': ICC staffer accuses chief prosecutor Karim Khan of sexual harassment
Japan’s abandoned rice fields are being restored into year-round wetlands to replenish groundwater and bring back frogs, dragonflies and endangered aquatic wildlife
stories.summary: Abandoned rice fields in Japan's Aso region are being restored into permanent wetlands to help refill groundwater and provide a safe habitat for frogs, dragonflies and other freshwater wildlife. The community-led project brings together local residents and researchers, showing how unused farmland can support biodiversity while helping restore water resources for the future.

stories.title: Congress rejects BJP-DMK alliance buzz as Stalin weighs stand on delimitation bill
stories.summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh denied any alliance between BJP and DMK due to differing ideologies. He stated that DMK remains an opposition party and is in contact with Congress MPs. DMK is studying the Delimitation Bill and will decide based on state interests. The party discussed seat increases and retaining current proportions among states. This decision will be made independently without consulting Congress.

stories.title: 'No beer in the cab': Florida woman stabs friend with scissors during argument
Pirates allegedly hijack chemical tanker Asana in Gulf of Aden off Yemen
How 'roadless rule' protects drinking water for 25M Americans
stories.summary: A new study reveals the Roadless Rule protects drinking water for twenty-five million Americans. This rule prevents development in national forests, safeguarding vital water sources. Removing protections could compromise water quality and increase treatment costs for utilities. These protected areas also support sensitive aquatic species and recreational opportunities. The U.S. Forest Service is currently reviewing public comments on the rule.

stories.title: 'Don't mix politics with ED': Madan Mitra denies notices to family prompted TMC faction switch
stories.summary: Madan Mitra has left Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress faction for a rebel group. He dismissed allegations that his decision was linked to the Enforcement Directorate's actions. Mitra stated his move was purely based on the current political landscape in West Bengal. He expressed disappointment with the TMC's strategy and leadership focus. Mitra also praised the political strength of Suvendu Adhikari.

stories.title: From prison to paradise: Once a dreaded prison island, this remote haven in Greece is now protecting one of the world's rarest seals
Trump alleges China interference in US elections amid suspicion he's prepping for mid-term loss
stories.summary: President Donald Trump alleged China compromised American election data extensively. He claimed Beijing illicitly acquired millions of US voter files. Critics questioned these claims, citing public data availability and intelligence assessments. Intelligence agencies concluded China did not attempt to alter vote counts. The timing of these allegations raised concerns among Republicans and Democrats.

stories.title: Odysseus helped the Greeks defeat Troy with a wooden horse, but his journey home became a 10-year fight against monsters, gods and fate
In 1980, Mount St Helens buried a river valley in volcanic sediment. Then 58 beavers helped turn the wasteland into a thriving wetland
stories.summary: More than 40 years after the Mount St. Helens eruption buried a Washington river valley under volcanic sediment, 58 relocated beavers have helped restore the damaged landscape. Their dams and wetlands brought back native plants, fish and wildlife. However, conservationists fear a planned government project to raise a sediment retention structure could undo years of natural restoration.

stories.title: 'Avoid unruly behaviour': CM Yogi says anti-social elements 'tarnishing' Kanwar Yatra
stories.summary: Addressing a function in Shamli district after inaugurating and laying the foundation stone for several development projects, CM Yogi said the state government was ensuring full security and all necessary arrangements for Kanwar pilgrims. "Today, no one stops the Kanwar Yatra. It is progressing peacefully and with enthusiasm. The government stands with the kanwariyas, and the administration and security forces are serving them," he was quoted as saying by news agency PTI.

stories.title: A campaign eliminated billions of sparrows to protect crops in 1958; the birds' disappearance accidentally triggered one of history's most devastating locust plagues
A Spanish company built a bladeless wind turbine that sways instead of spinning, turning the vibrations caused by wind into electricity
stories.summary: A Spanish company has developed bladeless wind turbines that oscillate to generate electricity. These devices use vortex-induced vibrations, a phenomenon engineers usually avoid. The bladeless design offers a lighter, quieter, and mechanically simpler alternative to traditional turbines. While currently less powerful, they are suited for small-scale and remote energy needs. This innovative technology could complement existing renewable energy solutions in the future.

stories.title: 'Modi thinks way in advance': PM says Hormuz crisis didn't affect Railways, draws parallel with 2014
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated Indian Railways' rapid electrification aids national energy security. Electrification over twelve years prevented a standstill during Middle East crises. Less than thirty percent of the rail network was electrified before 2014. Nearly ninety-nine percent of India's rail network is now electrified. This transformation ensures uninterrupted train operations despite global energy challenges.

stories.title: As wars destroyed schools and libraries across Italy, one Roman official began copying ancient books and helped save centuries of knowledge from disappearing
stories.summary: War in sixth-century Italy destroyed knowledge, prompting Cassiodorus to act. He founded a monastery where monks copied and translated manuscripts.
