This work saved religious and secular writings from being lost forever. The Vivarium monastery became a vital center for preserving ancient texts. Cassiodorus's efforts ensured knowledge survived centuries of instability.

stories.title: Russian recruits survive just 20-30 minutes on Ukraine frontlines: CIA chief explains why
stories.summary: Russian soldiers face a brief battlefield life expectancy of minutes. AI-powered drones have become specialized, low-cost killing machines on the front. Ukraine's mastery of drone warfare acts as a significant equalizer in the conflict. This technological advantage has helped Ukraine hold off Russia's superior force. Both sides have experienced substantial casualties since the invasion began.

stories.title: Dutch cities are replacing solid concrete surfaces with grass-filled paving blocks that absorb rainwater and help keep urban areas cooler
He had the money to buy a private jet, yet this billionaire preferred economy flights, took home free packets of salt and pepper from restaurants
stories.summary: IKEA founder Ingvar Kamprad lived a remarkably simple life despite his vast fortune. He consistently chose flea market clothes and economy travel, setting a personal example. Kamprad reused tea bags and ate at IKEA cafeterias, avoiding expensive dining options. His thrifty habits stemmed from his upbringing in rural southern Sweden. This frugality also shaped IKEA's company culture and employee guidelines.

stories.title: Not Philadelphia, this is where the United States started: Inside New Sweden, the long-lost colony that shaped America
stories.summary: Philadelphia's rich narrative isn't solely tied to its founding fathers' legacy; it also encompasses the short-lived Swedish colony of Nya Sverige. This settlement, which lasted seventeen years, pioneered the design of the log cabin, revolutionizing early American architecture. Furthermore, Swedish settlers introduced Lutheran Christianity and instigated critical early colonial rebellions, underscoring their significant yet brief impact in shaping America's foundations.

stories.title: Several trapped after landslide buries homes in China's Chongqing
stories.summary: State broadcaster CCTV said a local community worker noticed rocks falling from a hillside at around 8 am local time and issued an emergency warning. Authorities immediately began evacuating more than 60 residents, but the landslide struck at 9.08 am, trapping several people before the evacuation could be completed. Footage aired by CCTV showed a section of the hillside collapsing onto a cluster of riverside homes.

stories.title: 'If worry is about credit ...': Shiv Sena (UBT)'s Chaturvedi urges Centre to 'ease out' education minister
Scientists discovered a plastic-eating fungus in the Amazon rainforest that survives without oxygen and could one day help tackle landfill waste worldwide
Supreme Court clears all-India release of animated film 'Mahaprabhu Jagannath' after Rath Yatra festivities
'Risking life won't yield results': Pawan Khera as Wangchuk's hunger strike enters Day 20
'Demolition before court ruling amounts to SC contempt': Bhim Army’s Azad slams UP govt over proposed bulldozer action at Jauhar University
Gujarat ATS widens JeM crackdown, arrests 5 more in terror module probe
In New Jersey, cows named Blossom, Misty and Flurry graze beneath solar panels as scientists test whether one field can produce both food and clean energy
Japan tweaks imperial law but keeps throne male-only, barring women emperors
stories.summary: The legislation, passed by a large majority in the upper house, permits unmarried male descendants from former imperial branch families to be adopted back into the imperial household. It also allows female members of the imperial family to retain their royal status after marrying commoners, a privilege that was already available to male royals.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Arnold Schwarzenegger: "Just remember, you can't climb the ladder of success with…" - a powerful lesson on ambition, hard work and why success demands action
stories.summary: Arnold Schwarzenegger emphasized that success requires active effort, not just desire. His quote highlights the gap between ambition and actual work. Progress demands consistent action, which is more crucial than fleeting motivation. Breakthroughs often appear sudden but are built on years of preparation. This principle applies universally to any personal or professional aspiration.

stories.title: FBI arrests gangster Nitish Kaushal days after adding him to most wanted list
stories.summary: The FBI arrested Indian-origin Nitish Kaushal in Vermont as part of a crackdown. Kaushal is wanted for alleged involvement in murder and drug trafficking. He carried out violent acts for the Bhagwanpuria organised crime group. This arrest follows Operation Hard Ball targeting the Bhagwanpuria gang internationally. Federal prosecutors also charged Lawrence Bishnoi and Goldy Brar with ordering an assassination.

stories.title: Long-term exposure to air pollution could lead to dementia, warns WHO
stories.summary: New WHO guidelines suggest up to 45% of dementia cases are preventable. Tackling risk factors like high blood pressure and air pollution is advised. Healthy lifestyles and managing chronic diseases significantly influence brain health. The guidelines recommend regular physical activity and quitting tobacco use. Routine vitamin and omega-3 supplements are not advised without diagnosed deficiency.

stories.title: PF for self-employed, workers in unorganised sector on way
stories.summary: Employees Provident Fund Organisation is developing a universal provident fund scheme. This new plan will cover millions in the unorganised sector and self-employed individuals.

stories.title: Trump's teleprompter operator under federal probe over alleged $90,000 Kalshi insider trading bets
stories.summary: Donald Trump's teleprompter operator, Gabriel Perez, faces federal investigation for alleged insider trading. He is currently on unpaid leave from the White House after this development. The investigation focuses on trades made on prediction market platform Kalshi. Kalshi detected suspicious activity and alerted regulators, freezing Perez's account. Perez is reportedly cooperating with the ongoing federal inquiry into the matter.

stories.title: Unite to fight terror, organised crime, Ajit Doval urges Bimstec
stories.summary: NSA Ajit Doval chaired the Bimstec national security chiefs meeting in New Delhi. The grouping discussed practical solutions to combat terrorism and organized crime. Security chiefs also endorsed principles for maritime law enforcement interactions at sea. Doval stressed closer regional cooperation to tackle evolving security challenges effectively. Bimstec unites dynamic regions with significant global population and economic influence.

stories.title: Modi speaks to Qatar Amir, recalls legacy of his father
Call all-party meet to discuss delimitation bill: Kharge to PM Modi
stories.summary: Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge requested an all-party meeting with Prime Minister Modi. He seeks details on the revised Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill. Reports suggest the government plans to reintroduce the delimitation bill soon. Congress believes the government lacks the required majority for constitutional amendments. The party remains in touch with opposition parties regarding the bill.

stories.title: Govt plans bill to punish those who insult, block Vande Mataram singing
stories.summary: Delimitation, women's quota bills not on agenda yet

stories.title: No leak of Kudankulam nuclear reactor data, clarifies minister
stories.summary: Union minister Jitendra Singh asserted no sensitive data breach occurred at Kudankulam nuclear plant. Nuclear Power Corporation of India confirmed core systems remained untouched by the incident. Reliance Infrastructure's contract involved conventional services, not core nuclear systems. A third-party data center provider reported a partial data breach attempt. Isro sources clarified that scientist and engineer resignations are within normal levels.

stories.title: Skyroot Aerospace to launch India’s first private orbital rocket on Saturday
stories.summary: India's private space sector is poised for a significant advancement this Saturday. Skyroot Aerospace will launch the Vikram-1, its first orbital-class rocket. This historic mission, named Mission Aagaman, will lift off from Sriharikota. The rocket carries technology demonstration payloads and unique artwork into space. This launch marks a major milestone for India's burgeoning private space industry.

stories.title: 'Not a blanket bar': Supreme Court clarifies bulldozer order
stories.summary: The Supreme Court clarified its prior ruling on demolitions. Bulldozers can remove illegal constructions and encroachments on public land. This action requires strict adherence to municipal laws and procedures. Individual contempt petitions will be handled by jurisdictional High Courts. Fact-finding exercises will ascertain if authorities acted arbitrarily in demolitions.

stories.title: Avoid deploying sailors on vessels moving via Strait, DGMA tells companies
stories.summary: India's shipping regulator has advised against deploying seafarers in the Strait of Hormuz. This directive follows recent attacks on merchant vessels in the West Asia region. Two attacks on Tuesday involved commercial ships carrying thirty Indian seafarers. The directorate cited heightened security and ongoing conflict as reasons for enhanced measures. Fleet owners were previously asked to restrict seafarer deployment in this area.

stories.title: Acquitted 45 years on, after serving life term; murder in 1977, conviction 1981, clean chit 2026
stories.summary: The Supreme Court acquitted three surviving accused in a 49-year-old murder case. This decision came after the accused had served life imprisonment sentences. The court found serious infirmities in the prosecution's case and witness testimonies. Inconsistencies in witness accounts led to granting the benefit of doubt. The prosecution failed to establish guilt beyond reasonable doubt, leading to acquittal.

stories.title: Ukrainians protest Zelenskyy's ouster of his popular defense minister
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy reshuffled his wartime government, impacting key defense and prime ministerial roles. The defense minister's ouster sparked protests, highlighting friction with the military establishment. Ukraine's new prime minister, Serhii Koretskyi, leads the state energy company Naftogaz. These changes occur as Ukraine's fight against Russia continues with ongoing aerial attacks. The personnel overhaul tests Zelenskyy's political authority during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: 'Assassin' of B'desh ex-prez Ziaur Rehman held after 45 yrs
stories.summary: Former Bangladesh army Major Muzaffar Hossain has been arrested after forty-five years. He is allegedly a mastermind and assassin of President Ziaur Rahman. The arrest occurred in Dhaka's Banani DOHS area late Wednesday night. Hossain was reportedly handed over to the Bangladesh army for court martial. This marks a significant breakthrough for the current Tarique-led BNP government.

stories.title: US to revive rule of no green cards for those who use public benefits
Indian stabbed 15 times in a mall in US over his religion: Reports
stories.summary: An Indian man was allegedly stabbed fifteen times inside a Utah shopping mall. The suspect reportedly asked the victim his religion before the violent assault occurred. Authorities arrested the suspect on suspicion of attempted murder and carrying a dangerous weapon. The victim underwent surgery after being transported to a local hospital for treatment. The Indian consulate is in close contact with the victim's family and local authorities.

stories.title: Australian father and son were stranded in the outback for 12 hours rescued by a billionaire
stories.summary: A father and son from Melbourne found themselves lost for twelve hours in the stark South Australian outback after their vehicle sank into mud due to a fierce storm. Their fate caught the attention of billionaire Tim Roberts, who, after hearing their situation at a pub, took to the skies in his helicopter, teaming up with a local to locate and rescue them.

stories.title: Third language from Class IX will cause undue stress, says Supreme Court
Clavicular pushes back after AOC warns of ‘rabbit holes’ tied to growing looksmaxxing culture
stories.summary: Clavicular has responded after Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez shared concerns about looksmaxxing during an interview with TMZ. AOC said she worries about the pressures young men may face regarding appearance, while Clavicular argued that looksmaxxing is about improving multiple areas of life, including personality and charisma. Their comments have added to the wider debate around self-image and online influence.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Roman poet Virgil: 'If I cannot move Heaven, I will raise Hell', and a celebration of determination
NEET-UG results declared: 2 score 715/720, 19 cross 700
stories.summary: NEET-UG 2026 results revealed higher top scores following a nationwide retest. Aryan Gupta from Punjab secured the top position with a score of 715. Over 93% of candidates scoring above 690 were first-time test-takers. Women accounted for over 58% of the qualified candidates this year. The National Testing Agency declared results to keep medical admissions on track.

stories.title: Fema a civil law, RBI alone can compound offences, says ED
stories.summary: The Enforcement Directorate clarified Fema's role as civil legislation for voluntary compliance. Reserve Bank of India is the competent authority for compounding eligible contraventions. The ED issues a no-objection certificate to the central bank for compounding offenses. RBI recently closed a Fema case against Apothecon Pharmaceuticals after a penalty. This action follows master directions prescribing a compounding matrix for determining amounts.

stories.title: Does marital rape law shield men from unnatural sex prosecution?
stories.summary: The Supreme Court will examine if husbands can face charges for sexual acts causing harm. This question arises despite existing exemptions for marital rape under penal laws. The court will begin final hearings on these pending pleas from September ninth. The central issue is whether the court can create a new offense by striking down exceptions. The Centre opposes criminalizing marital rape, citing marriage as a unique relationship.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Richard Nixon: 'Always remember, others may hate you, but those who hate you don't win unless you hate them, and then you destroy yourself" and a lesson on how to deal with haters
Formulate policy to free elderly, terminally ill prisoners: Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court ordered states and Union Territories to create a policy for releasing elderly and terminally ill prisoners. This directive ensures constitutional values are upheld even within prison walls. The court emphasized that dignity and humane treatment remain paramount for all inmates. Data shows over 5,000 prisoners fall into these vulnerable categories. The policy must be formulated within the next three months.

stories.title: Quote of the day inspired by Ashoka: 'As long as there are people who approach the gods...'
stories.summary: Throughout history, the quest for immediate gratification has led to spiritual manipulation. Emperor Ashoka stood against those who exploited the fears and hopes of individuals, highlighting the transactional nature of faith. Today, the prosperity gospel and wellness movements reflect this enduring cycle. To escape this repetitive loop, we must recognize that genuine growth transcends simple transactions.

stories.title: No Green Card if you have used benefits like Medicaid, food stamps: Immigrants should not be burden on US
stories.summary: New Green Card rule: If applicants depend on government schemes like Medicaid, food stamps, they may not get Green Card as they will only become burden on the administration. Applicants must now prove they will not become financial burdens on the government. USCIS will publish a revised Form I-485 for these applications. The new rule takes effect on September 18, 2026.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Napoleon Bonaparte: 'The throne is only a piece of wood...'
stories.summary: Napoleon Bonaparte grasped that real power emerges from the collective imagination and faith of the people. He realized that symbols, like thrones, lack intrinsic authority. This principle of shared belief is fundamental to today’s economies and political structures. When public trust wanes, it leads to the depreciation of institutions and currencies. Ultimately, through the collective memory of society, Napoleon’s legend endured despite the fall of his empire.

stories.title: Amit Shah to review border security, law and order during three-day Bengal tour
stories.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah will visit West Bengal for three days starting Friday. He will review border security and governance matters during his important trip. Shah will interact with BSF personnel and inaugurate development projects near the border. Later, he will chair meetings on law and order and new criminal laws. The minister will also inaugurate a museum and lay a foundation stone for Amul Dairy.

stories.title: Omar Abdullah asks Centre to take humanitarian view on Wangchuk
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah expressed concern over Sonam Wangchuk's health. He urged the central government to adopt a humanitarian approach to the issue. Wangchuk has been fasting for nineteen days and has lost significant weight. Abdullah drew parallels with the UPA government's engagement with Anna Hazare. He stated Wangchuk's demand for NEET examination accountability was justified.

stories.title: Srinagar court grants NOC for passport to Farooq, sets conditions
stories.summary: A Srinagar court granted a no-objection certificate for Farooq Abdullah's passport. The court noted that pending criminal proceedings do not automatically bar travel. CBI had objected, fearing he might flee the country and evade justice. The passport was issued for one year, subject to conditions. Abdullah must seek permission before traveling outside Jammu and Kashmir.

stories.title: This ordinary pen helped save Apollo 11 astronauts, now it has sold at auction for an $857,600
stories.summary: A crucial felt-tip pen, famously utilized by Buzz Aldrin during the Apollo 11 mission, fetched an astonishing $857,600 at Sotheby's Space Exploration auction. This ordinary pen played a vital role in fixing a circuit breaker on the Moon, ensuring the lunar module's safe return to Earth. It exemplifies the ingenuity and urgent problem-solving that marked space exploration history.

stories.title: 'Take off uniform and contest elections': Pakistani MP's open challenge to its military
Centre puts Delhi hospitals on alert as Sonam Wangchuk fast enters third week
stories.summary: Central government hospitals will now conduct twice-daily health checks for hunger strikers. Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital is designated as the nodal facility for any emergencies. Advanced life support ambulances will remain stationed at the protest site. Medical teams will submit daily health status reports to the ministry. This action follows Delhi Police's request due to health concerns.

stories.title: NEET bounces back at the top: 19 cross 700, two score 715
4-year fixed stay for F1 students: Immigration attorney says the biggest risk is 'booking a flight home', warns visa holders against traveling outside US
Henry Nowak murder: UK Police translate Sikh man Vickrum Digwa's murder confession to brother Gurpreet
'No sensitive data leaked': Government refutes reports of Kudankulam nuclear plant breach
stories.summary: Union Minister Jitendra Singh dismissed reports of sensitive Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant files being leaked. He asserted that no nuclear safety or security data had been compromised in the incident. The Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited clarified leaked documents related only to the plant's conventional Balance of Plant package. This clarification followed claims by a ransomware group about accessing thousands of project-related files.

stories.title: 30 convicted in Genoa bridge collapse after eight years
Who is Suki Mellow? Kai Cenat calls out content creator over alleged Jasontheween stalking at Streamer University
stories.summary: Suki Mellow is a Texas-based Twitch streamer known for Just Chatting and IRL content. She became a talking point at Streamer University 2026 after Kai Cenat jokingly referenced videos involving Jasontheween and warned her about allegedly stalking him. Suki denied the claim. Another clip later showed her searching for Jasontheween and discussing his relationship status with Yonna Jay.

stories.title: Scientists tracked 6,000 penguin dives beneath Antarctic sea ice and found that...
stories.summary: In recent times, penguins face challenges in sourcing food due to altered prey behaviors. As krill and fish migrate deeper or spread out to elude predators, penguins must dive greater depths and swim longer distances in search of sustenance. Thus, it's crucial for conservation initiatives to take into account these changing hunting dynamics in our evolving oceans.

stories.title: 'More people will leave TMC because of dictatorship': Ritabrata Banerjee after Koel Mullick's Rajya Sabha exit
'500 farmers join CJP protest': Sonam Wangchuk gets support from Rakesh Tikait, Kejriwal at 'packed' Jantar Mantar
stories.summary: Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike entered its nineteenth day with significant health concerns. Farmer leader Rakesh Tikait joined the protest, strengthening the ongoing agitation. Opposition leaders and parties offered their support, urging the minister's removal. Congress leaders appealed to Wangchuk to end his fast while assuring continued demands. Doctors warned of serious health complications if the hunger strike continues.

stories.title: Streamer University 2026: Valkyrae’s ‘d*mmy mommy’ classroom idea sparks curiosity ahead of Kai Cenat event
stories.summary: Valkyrae has shared both her teaching plans and course details ahead of Streamer University 2026. Speaking on the Wine About It podcast, she described a playful classroom idea featuring rewards and punishments for students. She also revealed that her course will focus on building a brand beyond streaming and announced that she has landed another movie role.

stories.title: Spain is turning olive pits into road material that could cut asphalt emissions
stories.summary: Barcelona is testing olive pit biochar for sustainable road construction. This innovative asphalt mixture reduces emissions by approximately seventy-five percent. Olive pits are converted into biochar through a process called pyrolysis. This material locks carbon within the road infrastructure for decades. The project aims to create long-term carbon storage assets in urban areas.

stories.title: NRI wife says neighbor called cops when she and her husband were arguing: 'Police took my husband to the station, I don't know what to do'
stories.summary: An Indian woman in Texas sought help on social media after her husband was taken by the police based on the complaint of a neighbor who also told the police that the husband frequently shouted at the wife. The wife said when police came they saw minor injury on her as she was pushed during the argument.

stories.title: 'Everyone does naarebaazi in democracy but ... ': Why Supreme Court told Chandigarh admin to 'argue on merits' in Bhagwant Mann case
stories.summary: The Supreme Court will hear the Chandigarh administration's plea regarding an FIR. This FIR was against Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and other AAP leaders. The High Court had previously quashed the FIR, citing a lack of prima facie case. The protest in 2020 was against a hike in electricity tariffs. The court noted that sloganeering is common in a democracy.

stories.title: For 150 years, silos shaped the Corn Belt landscape. Now one woman has tracked nearly 200 built by her grandfather before they disappear
stories.summary: Towering concrete silos once defined the American Corn Belt landscape. Modern farming has led to the decline of these traditional structures. One woman is documenting nearly two hundred silos built by her grandfather. This effort preserves an important part of agricultural history and rural craftsmanship. These efforts ensure earlier generations' work will not be forgotten.

stories.title: Japan midwife killed patient with feces-tainted IV, phone history reveals sickening searches
How to protect yourself around dangerous North American wild animals: Essential safety tips for your national park visit
stories.summary: Outdoor adventurers can safely enjoy wildlife by staying alert and traveling in groups. Defensive bears may moan or swat the ground, requiring a slow retreat. Predatory bears demand an aggressive stance and a fight if attacked. Mountain lions require showing you are a danger, not a meal. Large herbivores like moose also need ample space and respect from visitors.

stories.title: US designates 2 Mexican cartels as foreign terror groups, expands crackdown on drug networks
Duration of US visa stay changes - what it means for foreign students, exchange visitors and journalists
Gallup CEO Jon Clifton warns: Elon Musk’s Mars vision may become reality before fixing the global workplace productivity crisis costing $10 trillion
11,000 drivers in California will have to retake written test, DMV says they suspect cheating
stories.summary: California's Department of Motor Vehicles has declared 11,000 knowledge tests invalid due to suspicions of cheating. To maintain their licenses, motorists are required to retake their written exams within 30 days. The DMV uncovered anomalies in the results through regular internal checks, emphasizing that these discrepancies stem from test takers rather than technical issues.

stories.title: 'Congress in touch with all opposition parties, including DMK and AAP': Jairam Ramesh on delimitation bill
stories.summary: Congress is contacting opposition parties that previously opposed a bill. These discussions include the DMK and Aam Aadmi Party. Parliament's Monsoon session begins July 20 and continues until August 13. Opposition plans to raise issues like the NEET paper leak. The government may also reintroduce a bill on women's reservation.

stories.title: Scientists showed horses silent videos of wolves and found their hearts raced even when...
stories.summary: Horses exhibit an intriguing phenomenon when identifying predators on video screens—they experience heightened heart rates indicative of internal stress while showing no outward signs of fear. Notably, male horses and dominant herd members trigger stronger responses, challenging traditional views of prey animals' panic-driven behavior. Grasping this psychological disconnect is essential for improving horse welfare and ensuring rider safety.

stories.title: Old playbook that made Channi Punjab CM in 2021 is back in action. Why Congress may not blink this time
stories.summary: Congress leadership struggles to unite Punjab leaders amid ongoing internal disputes. New leadership structure has triggered open conflict and fresh rounds of infighting. Former Chief Minister Charanjit Singh Channi is now leading a revolt against the current party president. The party leadership appears firm this time, avoiding past mistakes of succumbing to pressure. Managing these divisions is critical for Congress to regain political ground in Punjab.

stories.title: Sea Shepherd chased Japan's whalers for years but ultimately lost the battle
'Extreme brutality': Pakistan's PTI to launch nationwide protests for Imran Khan's release
Scientists are turning air filters into DNA collectors that can detect traces of viruses
stories.summary: Innovative scientists have developed a method to analyze airborne environmental DNA using standard air filters. This groundbreaking technology can detect local wildlife and monitor viruses without the need for direct observation. Existing national air pollution monitoring stations are already harnessing this essential biological data. Utilizing advanced sequencing techniques, researchers can map entire ecosystems and explore genetic variations within species.

stories.title: Scientists found South America’s first insect-bearing amber, a 112-million-year-old time capsule from a lost dinosaur-era forest
Texas floods: Evacuations begin across Hill Country as forecasters warn of 'deadly wave'
Kejriwal's 'Sheesh Mahal' to guest house: Delhi govt may rope in private firm to run bungalow
stories.summary: The Delhi government plans to convert Arvind Kejriwal's former residence into a state guest house. A private hospitality firm may operate and maintain the bungalow for revenue generation. This repurposed building will accommodate traveling ministers and government officials for a fee. A portion of the camp office will host official events like seminars and meetings. The proposal awaits final approval from higher authorities for implementation.

stories.title: 'Make Sonam Wangchuk education minister': Arvind Kejriwal joins Jantar Mantar protest, seeks Dharmendra Pradhan's ouster
stories.summary: Arvind Kejriwal joined Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike at Jantar Mantar. He demanded the removal of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Kejriwal also endorsed Wangchuk as a potential replacement for the minister. He highlighted recurring exam paper leaks and student suicides. The former Delhi CM urged the government to listen to youth concerns.

stories.title: MIT built a 300-gram robot that flies through the sky, dives underwater and takes off again, just like a diving bird
stories.summary: The Flapping-wing Aerial-aquatic Vehicle (FAAV), developed by engineers at MIT and EPFL, is a 300-gram robot designed to mimic the diving birds like the Atlantic puffin. It is the first machine capable of completing the full cycle of swimming, diving, and launching back into the sky using its wings rather than separate propellers or legs.

stories.title: How concretisation is turning cities into monsoon flood traps
stories.summary: Urban regions are increasingly battling monsoon flooding, exacerbated by extensive concretisation. With impermeable surfaces dominating, rainwater struggles to seep in, leading to heightened runoff. Meanwhile, the decline of natural water reservoirs like wetlands further complicates the situation. In response, authorities are encouraging the use of permeable materials and green spaces. While initiatives for de-concretisation are on the rise, the swift pace of construction poses significant hurdles.

stories.title: 'Cabinet expansion very soon': Congress hints at Karnataka reshuffle after Rahul-DKS meeting
stories.summary: Karnataka cabinet expansion is expected to occur very soon. Senior Congress leaders met in Delhi to discuss the long-pending cabinet appointments. Consultations are underway to fill twenty vacant ministerial positions and the Speaker's post. The party aims to balance regional and caste equations for the selections. This expansion is anticipated before the upcoming assembly session begins in August.

stories.title: Scientists listen for alien signals on K2-18b but detect only cosmic silence
Meet Vaibhav Bhaskar, an Indian-origin student who broke Florida's high school record with 11.99 GPA
stories.summary: Achieving a stunning 11.99 GPA, Indian-origin Vaibhav Bhaskar has rewritten the record books for Florida high schools. His extraordinary performance sparked a critical review of grading practices, acadmic burnout of students. Vaibhav said he was not burned out but tired and now it felt surreal that suddenly he did not have anything to do after his high school graduation.

stories.title: 'Brazenly working like a BJP branch office': Derek O'Brien slams ECI over extensions to rebel TMC faction
Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun yet Venus is hotter; thanks to a runaway greenhouse effect
Jeff Bezos's wife could not afford a prom dress growing up. Now she and the Amazon founder are...
stories.summary: In a significant philanthropic move, Lauren Sanchez and Jeff Bezos have pledged $34 million towards cutting-edge sustainable textile research. This funding aims to advance the creation of biodegradable fibers and plastic-free synthetic silk. For Sanchez, this initiative is particularly meaningful, having faced personal hardships in her youth. The couple also toasted their first wedding anniversary aboard their luxurious superyacht, amplifying their commitment to environmental conservation and community support.

stories.title: Puri Rath Yatra: One killed, over 100 devotees faint amid massive crowd
An Australian cyclist accidentally trapped a 2-metre venomous eastern brown snake in her bike chain, then it bit her
Pluto's moon Charon may have once spun once every 14 hours, and its ancient mountains still record how it slowed down
stories.summary: New research suggests Charon's oldest landscapes preserve evidence of early despinning. Tectonic features in Oz Terra indicate a period of faster rotation for the moon. These structures resemble landforms created by crustal compression, which is consistent with despinning models. Scientists estimate Charon's initial rotation period was approximately fourteen hours. This ancient process likely occurred before other major geological events reshaped its surface.

stories.title: Beheading of Indian-origin motel manager in Dallas: Prosecutors say they won't seek death penalty against accused
stories.summary: Prosecutors have opted against seeking the death penalty for Yordanis Cobos-Martinez in the grim case of motel manager Chandra Nagamallaiah's murder. Allegations point to a fierce quarrel that culminated in Martinez allegedly beheading Nagamallaiah, with harrowing footage documenting the act. Should he be found guilty, Martinez will face life behind bars without the possibility of parole.

stories.title: Border infra to play indispensable role in future: Rajnath; lauds BRO for adopting niche tech to build world-class infra
SCBA urges Wangchuk to end fast, regrets non-responsive institutional conscience
'Those under pressure, go wherever you want': Mamata as TMC exodus continues with Koel Mallick's exit
stories.summary: Mamata Banerjee addressed the Trinamool Congress exodus after the recent assembly poll defeat. She suggested leaders facing pressure are free to leave the party. Rajya Sabha MP Koel Mallick resigned, adding to the growing list of exits. This resignation followed Madan Mitra quitting to join a rebel TMC faction. Banerjee also defended her nephew Abhishek Banerjee amid internal party issues.

stories.title: Evening newswrap: Kharge writes to PM over revised delimitation proposal; Falklands poster row spills over after World Cup clash, and more
Did Kushner, Witkoff profit from Middle East war? What Iran claimed in private message to Vance
Iceland heats every home using energy from volcanoes, and almost all of its electricity comes from renewable sources, making it one of the world's cleanest energy systems
More than 60 artisans have spent over two decades building a castle like it's 1230; it's still not finished
stories.summary: A French historical experiment began building a medieval castle in 1997. Skilled craftspeople use only hand tools and traditional methods for construction. This remarkable project has become a major tourist attraction and research center. Workers learn by studying ruins and experimenting with historical techniques. The castle remains unfinished after over twenty-five years of dedicated work.

stories.title: A 67-million-year-old T. rex discovered on a South Dakota ranch has sold for $50.1 million, becoming the most expensive dinosaur fossil ever auctioned
'We'll go to Delhi and raise our voice': Omar Abdullah vows to press for J&K statehood demand
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah confirmed a planned protest in Delhi. The National Conference will demonstrate on July 20 for statehood restoration. He stated the protest program will proceed as scheduled. The venue or format of the demonstration may change, he noted. Abdullah declined to label the permission delay as sabotage.

stories.title: 'We share your anguish and outrage': Congress reaches out to Sonam Wangchuk in first reaction to hunger strike
stories.summary: Congress has appealed to activist Sonam Wangchuk to end his hunger strike. The party shares his concerns over the education minister's accountability. Wangchuk has been fasting for nineteen days demanding the minister's resignation. Congress assures continued pressure for the education minister's removal. The party supports the activist's demand for accountability in education.

stories.title: 211 patients undergoing chemo evacuated: US strikes near Iran cancer hospital for children - video
Quote of the day by the Dalai Lama: "Good human qualities… honesty, sincerity, a good heart, cannot be bought with money, nor can they be produced by machines, but…"
stories.summary: Inner human qualities like honesty and a good heart are essential. These qualities cannot be bought with money or produced by machines. They are cultivated by the mind and form the essence of humanity. Visible achievements and material wealth do not define true character. Genuine human connection relies on these deeply ingrained values.

stories.title: Guam kingfishers vanished from their home after invasive snakes devastated their species: Now scientists are restoring them with four new chicks
stories.summary: The Guam Kingfisher, known as 'sihek', is extinct in the wild due to invasive brown tree snakes. These birds played vital roles in the island's ecosystem, controlling insect populations. Their disappearance has led to increased spider numbers and thinner forests on Guam. Conservation centers now house the remaining 140 birds, aiming for eventual reintroduction. Efforts focus on breeding pairs to save this species from complete extinction.

stories.title: A woman with a Stanford PhD in mathematics has been claimed to have cracked the lottery algorithm after winning the lottery four times and collecting more than $20 million
'No further delay': Delhi HC gives Kejriwal, AAP leaders final chance to file replies in excise policy case
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court granted AAP leaders a final chance to file their replies. This pertains to the CBI's revision petition challenging a trial court order. Arvind Kejriwal, Manish Sisodia, and Durgesh Pathak are the respondents in this matter. The court emphasized no further adjournments would be granted for these filings. The case has been listed for further hearing on August 17 and 18.

stories.title: 'Manmohan govt engaged with Anna Hazare ... ': Omar Abdullah says Centre unmoved by Sonam Wangchuk
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah supports Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike. Wangchuk is protesting alleged irregularities in the NEET examination, demanding accountability. His health has significantly deteriorated after nineteen days of fasting. Doctors warn of serious health complications if the hunger strike continues. The Delhi High Court has ordered daily medical examinations for Wangchuk.

stories.title: Around 2 billion years ago, Oklo became a natural nuclear reactor beneath Africa, and its radioactive remains are still there
'Convene an all-party meeting': Kharge writes to PM Modi on revised Delimitation Bill ahead of Monsoon session
stories.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to call an all-party meeting. He requested adequate time for opposition parties to study the revised delimitation proposals. The Congress party plans to strongly oppose the proposed delimitation bill if reintroduced. They will also work to maintain unity among all opposition parties. The party supports women's reservation but opposes linking it to delimitation.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Kate Middleton: "People often ask me why I am so interested in the mental health of children and young people. The answer is…" - a powerful message on childhood mental health and why early support can shape a lifetime
stories.summary: Kate Middleton emphasizes that every child deserves the best possible start in life. This involves nurturing emotional well-being, not just addressing crises. Early years are vital for developing trust and security in children. Children often show distress indirectly, requiring adult awareness and patience. Providing emotional foundations helps children face life's challenges with confidence.

stories.title: 'Act now': Indian teen Romanch Mahajan's father urges NYC to ban horse carriages after son's death
Ukraine gets new PM: Parliament approves Serhii Koretskyi amid cabinet shuffle
stories.summary: Ukraine's parliament approved Serhii Koretskyi as the new prime minister on Thursday. This appointment follows the resignation of former prime minister Yulia Svyrydenko. President Zelenskyy cited Koretskyi's energy sector experience for winter preparations. The government reshuffle includes other senior officials and aims to refresh leadership. Mykhailo Fedorov's dismissal as defense minister sparked protests and criticism.

stories.title: Southern California is being paid up to $65 million to leave 65 billion gallons of water for it
stories.summary: Historically low water levels are plaguing Lake Mead, affecting millions in various states and Mexico. To combat this, federal funds will support efforts to keep water in the reservoir this year, coupled with initiatives aimed at conserving agricultural water annually. While these measures are crucial for now, achieving lasting change will necessitate cooperation among Colorado River Basin states regarding future water management.

stories.title: An ancient sea once divided North America from north to south; 70-million-year-old creatures from its waters still shimmer like gemstones
stories.summary: Millions of years ago, South Dakota was covered by a vast inland sea. This ancient seaway supported diverse marine life, including ammonites and marine reptiles. Today, fossils from this period are displayed at the Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History. These ancient shells still shine due to their mother-of-pearl composition. Discoveries continue to reveal insights into prehistoric marine ecosystems and Earth's history.

stories.title: ED raids 13 locations across four states in money laundering probe linked to Bangladeshi-Rohingya infiltration
stories.summary: The Enforcement Directorate conducted searches across four states in a money laundering investigation. This probe targets a syndicate facilitating illegal infiltration of foreign nationals into India. Public charitable trusts registered under FCRA are suspected of receiving foreign funds. These funds were allegedly diverted through multiple accounts to aid illegal immigrants. The investigation stems from an FIR registered by the Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorist Squad.

stories.title: NIA court reserves order on Baramulla MP Rashid Sheikh's plea to attend Parliament in custody
stories.summary: A Baramulla MP has requested court permission to attend the upcoming Parliament session. He is currently in judicial custody for a terror funding case investigation. The National Investigation Agency stated it has no objection to his attendance. The court heard arguments from the MP's counsel and the NIA. An order on this petition is expected later today.

stories.title: From 'chanda chori' to paper leaks & inflation: Congress to target Modi govt over key issues in Monsoon Session, will oppose Delimitation Bill
Bumblebees survive pesticide exposure, but reproductive genes begin changing
Another setback for TMC, Koel Mallick resigns from Rajya Sabha
stories.summary: TMC leader Koel Mallik resigned from the Rajya Sabha on Thursday. This follows Madan Mitra's departure and joining a rebel TMC faction. Earlier, Sukhendu Sekhar Ray and Sushmita Dev also resigned from the party. They subsequently joined the Bharatiya Janata Party and filed nomination papers. The BJP defended its decision to field these former TMC leaders.

stories.title: Norway is drilling the world's longest and deepest undersea road tunnel through fault zones and rock that keeps letting seawater in
'Earlier, the better': Why SC wants Centre to rethink third language policy from class 9
Japan is building floating wind turbines far out at sea because its waters become too deep for traditional turbines
A Maya astronomer studied the movements of Venus and Mars in AD 781, and archaeologists have now discovered his name
Punjab Congress divided as every leader wants to be CM: Mann
stories.summary: Addressing a public gathering in Mukerian, he said the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government had fulfilled its promises through initiatives in education, healthcare, power and social welfare, and urged people to give the party another mandate so that "opportunist" opposition leaders, especially the Congress, do not get a chance to come to power.

stories.title: During Tanzania's deadly 1993 drought, an elephant matriarch's memory helped save her entire herd, while a younger leader stayed behind and more calves died
Meet Julia Butterfly Hill: The 23-year-old woman who climbed a 1,000-year-old tree and stayed there for 738 days to save it from being cut down
A $22.5 million Montauk teardown shack sits next to Robert De Niro’s estate, but the real prize is its rare oceanfront lot and approved plans for a 7,100-square-foot luxury home
stories.summary: An oceanfront Montauk property is listed for twenty-two point five million dollars. This desirable location sits adjacent to Robert De Niro's estate and offers unique advantages. The sale includes approved plans for a large modern home, bypassing lengthy permit processes. This property provides an opportunity to build a significant residence on one point one acres. The site offers incredible ocean views, similar to those found in Malibu.

stories.title: 'New language in class 9 stressful': SC on CBSE's compulsory 3-language decision
stories.summary: "No that is very bad. 9th standard is stressful. Why do you introduce a new language in 9th? You introduce it in 6th. When we were there in our school we had both ICSE and SSLC. We were taught both syllabus. Only at the end of 9th standard we had to select," Justice BV Nagarathna, who was hearing plea challenging Madras high court direction to establish Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas in each district, said according to Live Law.

stories.title: Emperor penguins survive Antarctica's brutal winters by huddling together, but a maths study reveals the hidden system behind their remarkable teamwork
stories.summary: Emperor penguins in Antarctica form huddles to survive extreme cold temperatures. Each penguin moves to reduce its own heat loss, which benefits the entire group. This movement ensures every bird eventually experiences the warmer center of the huddle. The study modeled this behaviour, showing it explains even warmth distribution. Researchers found this natural movement is key to their survival strategy.

stories.title: 'Give us the choice': AAP opposes mandatory E20 Petrol, launches public petition
Scientists have finally explained why killer whales struggle to hear blue whales, and the answer may have helped the giants survive for millions of years
stories.summary: Some baleen whales use low-frequency songs to avoid killer whales. This acoustic crypsis helps flight species escape predators in open oceans. Blue whales, known for loud calls, sing at frequencies predators cannot hear. Natural selection favored these low-frequency calls over millions of years. This discovery reveals how predation shaped whale communication systems.

stories.title: Sean 'Diddy' Combs sells $55 million Miami mansion he used as bail collateral in sex trafficking case
stories.summary: Sean Combs sold a Miami mansion for fifty-five million dollars. This waterfront property was previously offered as bail collateral. Homeland Security agents had searched the estate during an investigation. Combs was convicted on two counts and sentenced to prison. He is currently serving his sentence while his appeal is pending.

stories.title: Germany's fossil-rich limestone reveals a new 150-million-year-old flying reptile
stories.summary: Scientists in Germany have identified a new ancient flying reptile species. This nearly complete fossil dates back approximately 150 million years. The creature, named Laueropterus vitriolus, had a wingspan of about one meter. Its preservation offers insights into ancient environments and prehistoric animal communities. This discovery highlights ongoing learning about prehistoric life globally.

stories.title: In 1968, John Calhoun created the perfect home for eight mice. The colony grew to more than 2,200 before it slowly vanished
40-gram, palm-sized AI micro-drone kills a flying insect autonomously in mid-air for the first time. Now it could eradicate mosquitoes and save thousands of lives
China's 125-million-year-old dinosaur fossil reveals preserved skin, strange spikes and a previously unknown species
'Life is precious': Delhi HC urges Centre to regularly examine Sonam Wangchuk's health
stories.summary: Hearing the a PIL over fasting activist's dwindling health, the high court noted that ​​"life is precious" and asked both the governments to provide, if needed, medical aid, to the Ladakh native. Doctors have warned that Wangchuk may soon enter a potentially "alarming" phase involving organ damage. Wangchuk has reportedly lost more than 9kgs since beginning his indefinite hunger strike.

stories.title: Meet Marvin Minsky: MIT professor who predicted today's Anthropic-style multi-agent AI nearly 40 years ago and became the founding father of artificial intelligence
SC to hear plea against Orissa HC stay on 'Mahaprabhu Jagannath' film
stories.summary: The development comes a day after the Shree Jagannath Temple Managing Committee (SJTMC) urged the makers to postpone the film's release, alleging that it presents a fictional version of the deity's life that is inconsistent with Hindu scriptures. The appeal was made by Gajapati Maharaja Dibyasingha Deb, the titular king of Puri and chairman of the SJTMC, the highest decision-making body of the 12th-century Jagannath Temple.

stories.title: At least 500 Rohingya feared dead after two boats capsize in Bay of Bengal
stories.summary: Two boats carrying Rohingya people capsized in the Bay of Bengal. At least 500 individuals are feared dead after these tragic incidents. The boats departed from Myanmar's Rakhine state and Bangladesh refugee camps. These perilous sea crossings occur during the dangerous monsoon season. The international community is urged to increase support for Rohingya refugees.

stories.title: 'This isn't a paper leak—it's theft': Rahul Gandhi ahead of Dehradun leg of 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' on July 17
NPCIL denies nuclear systems breach after Kudankulam data leak report
stories.summary: India's Nuclear Power Corporation stated a data breach involves conventional plant facilities. The reported leaked files pertain only to non-nuclear safety systems. These documents were prepared by Reliance Infrastructure Ltd. for common services. The breach does not compromise nuclear security or reactor core systems. The affected information relates to plant units under construction.

stories.title: 'Could be alarming': Doctor flag new 'risks' as Sonam Wangchuk loses over 9kgs, fast enters Day 19
Quote of the day by Diego Maradona: "I made mistakes, and I paid for them. But…" - the football legend's powerful message about mistakes and redemption
stories.summary: Diego Maradona's famous quote separates personal mistakes from the game's purity. He admitted his errors and paid consequences for them. The ball, representing football, remained untouched by his personal failings. This distinction highlights how a person's flaws do not destroy their passion. Maradona's words endure by acknowledging complexity without offering simple excuses.

stories.title: 'Don't let BJP change narrative': Mahua Moitra's message to Wangchuk over LoP Rahul Gandhi 's absence from protest
NASA's Curiosity Rover spots mysterious honeycomb pattern on Mars
Not just nostalgia value: Why Kolkata wants its trams back
stories.summary: Once dismissed as slow and obsolete, trams are returning globally as clean urban transport. India’s last surviving network now has a second chance, writes Krishnendu Bandyopadhyay

stories.title: India’s next big reform is where we live
stories.summary: India’s urban centers hold the key to its economic progress, demanding smart planning and investment to thrive. Three pivotal reforms — targeting regional hubs and essential infrastructure — can ignite urban potential for overall national development. By addressing housing regulations, cities can welcome private investment, while refined governance and finance structures will empower urban areas to offer outstanding public services.

stories.title: 'They better behave': Trump says Iran wants settlement amid fresh strikes
stories.summary: President Trump warned Iran to behave if it desires negotiations with Washington. US forces conducted new military strikes targeting Iranian command centers and air defense systems. These strikes aimed to degrade Iran's ability to threaten commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian authorities reported a missile attack near a cancer hospital in Ahvaz. Damage was also reported at an industrial facility in Qeshm following an enemy attack.

stories.title: Nasa warns: Many US coastal cities could go underwater by 2050
FDA raids Siya Goyal's father's shop, seizes food products worth over Rs 8 lakh
'Not in good shape but ...': Sonam Wangchuk refuses to end fast despite health concerns
stories.summary: Sonam Wangchuk continues his hunger strike for nineteen days, stating his health is not critical. He urged supporters to join a Parliament march on July 20 instead of asking him to break his fast. Wangchuk believes his protest sends a message about government accountability and the need for action. His health has been monitored, and medical tests show stable results for his condition.

stories.title: 'Mossad or CIA': Vance hints at Epstein link to Israeli intel; admits Trump admin 'screwed up' handling of files
stories.summary: JD Vance admitted that the Trump administration mishandled the communication surrounding the release of the Jeffrey Epstein files, blaming much of the confusion on former Attorney General Pam Bondi's public remarks. He also defended Donald Trump against allegations of trying to suppress the documents and suggested that intelligence agencies like Mossad or CIA had connections to Epstein.

stories.title: 'To keep troops at absolute best': US announces annual testosterone screening for service members
stories.summary: US defense secretary Pete Hegseth announced a new annual testosterone screening program. This initiative will target military personnel aged thirty and older for better performance. Service members under thirty can volunteer for testing, while therapy remains voluntary. Medical experts note testosterone decline with age, impacting various health aspects, while critics question the policy.

stories.title: 'Like my lover': Chinese users bid farewell to AI companions
stories.summary: China's new regulations took effect Wednesday, curbing emotional dependency on AI companions. Major AI providers suspended custom agent and companion features ahead of the deadline. Users expressed deep grief on social media, archiving chat histories and sharing last conversations. These rules target AI tools with anthropomorphic traits, prohibiting virtual partners for minors. Services not involving ongoing emotional interaction are exempt from these new measures.

stories.title: Oil prices extend gain for fourth day, stay beyond $85 amid Middle East chaos
stories.summary: Crude oil prices climbed for a fourth day, exceeding eighty-five dollars per barrel. Investors reacted to escalating United States and Iran conflict and shipping route security. United States strikes on Iran's missile sites and coastal defense positions occurred. This intensified worries over oil moving through the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts suggest prices could rise further depending on conflict developments.

stories.title: TVS arm Home Credit to buy education loan company for Rs 967 crore
stories.summary: Home Credit India will acquire Varthana Finance in an all-cash deal valued at Rs 967 crore. This transaction will make Varthana a wholly owned subsidiary of Home Credit India. The acquisition aims to diversify portfolios and improve business mix for the company. It is expected to create synergies in distribution, technology, and risk management. Regulatory approvals are required, with completion anticipated within nine months.

stories.title: Ficci chief: It's for industry to take advantage of FTAs
stories.summary: Economic momentum sustains as oil prices moderate and trade deals offer new opportunities. Corporate sector performance shows robust demand, with automotive and banking sectors leading growth. Manufacturing faces margin stress due to inventory, while IT remains under pressure. Industry is preparing for increased demand, with capacity additions planned after reaching utilization levels. Concerns about Chinese dumping necessitate a stronger trade defense mechanism for fair competition.

stories.title: 35 years on, 103-yr-old woman wins legal battle for plot of land
stories.summary: Habiban Khatoon, aged 103, finally received justice after a 35-year legal battle. Her eldest son purchased land in her name, but a cousin took possession. She filed a title suit in 1994, facing appeals up to the High Court. After years of proceedings and delays, she regained possession of her land. The long legal fight incurred significant financial costs for Habiban.

stories.title: Patna high court ruling on groping draws criticism from top court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court expressed serious concern over a Patna High Court order. This order stated that removing a woman's salwar did not constitute attempted rape. The apex court emphasized judges must research and follow its previous rulings. It directed all courts to adhere to judicial sensitivity guidelines. States will issue instructions to police stations regarding FIR registration and chargesheets.

stories.title: Clavicular's Israel visit ends in controversy as IDF sidelines soldier over livestream with controversial streamer
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces removed soldier Shira Braun from its international communications unit and imposed a suspended jail sentence after she appeared in a livestream with controversial influencer Braden "Clavicular" Peters. The IDF said the action was based on her conduct, not misuse of official systems. Peters, known for his ties to polarizing internet figures and controversial content, drew criticism during his Israel visit, prompting debate over military standards, influencer culture, and institutional accountability.

stories.title: Move high court on SIR-linked ration card cancellation: Supreme Court to petitioner
stories.summary: The Supreme Court declined to hear a petition regarding ration card cancellations. These cancellations followed voter list deletions due to doubtful citizenship status. The court directed the petitioner to pursue his appeal before the relevant tribunal. A favorable tribunal outcome would reinstate his name on the electoral roll. The issue of linking deletions to ration card cancellations must be challenged in the High Court.

stories.title: BJP turns PM Modi visits to states into 'swachh' drives
stories.summary: Organized cleanliness drives now precede Prime Minister Modi's state visits across India. These initiatives transform pre-VVIP spruce-ups into public campaigns involving citizens and officials. Haryana launched a statewide drive ahead of Prime Minister Modi's upcoming visit to Jind. Similar campaigns were observed in Odisha and West Bengal during recent visits. The true success of these drives will be measured by sustained cleanliness after the visits conclude.

stories.title: 2022 in mind, Congress may continue with Amarinder Raja Warring as Punjab party chief
stories.summary: The Congress party is not favoring a leadership change in its Punjab unit. This stance comes despite some functionaries demanding Amarinder Raja Warring's removal. Party leaders are wary of reversing recent appointments, which caused internal backlash. Dissidence presents a difficult situation for the Congress party ahead of polls. The party may try to persuade dissidents with assurances and future promises.

stories.title: Nearly 10,000 more MBBS seats up for grabs this year
stories.summary: India's MBBS capacity reaches a record 1,36,939 seats for the 2026-27 academic session. This expansion is driven by new regulations allowing earlier seat increase applications. The National Medical Commission approved 9,911 additional undergraduate seats across the nation. These new seats include those in newly established and existing medical colleges. Private institutions contributed significantly to this substantial increase in medical seats.

stories.title: PM Modi & Shah 'discuss BJP organisational overhaul'
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with Home Minister Amit Shah and BJP chief Nitin Nabin. Discussions focused on the party's upcoming list of office-bearers and potential ministerial changes. The new team under Nitin Nabin is expected to be announced soon by the party. An overhaul of national organizational bodies, including the parliamentary board, is also anticipated. These deliberations signal significant upcoming shifts within the BJP's leadership structure.

stories.title: Delay may make registrations of birth, deaths tough
stories.summary: Delayed birth and death registrations may soon require judicial magistrate orders. The government proposes this change to tighten the existing registration process. Reporting births and deaths after two years will need judicial approval. This aims to ensure near real-time recording and prevent misuse. The proposed amendment was placed before the Cabinet for consideration.

stories.title: Blake Neff blasts Candace Owens’ ‘Russian spy project’ claim, questions evidence behind TPUSA allegations
stories.summary: Candace Owens recently questioned alleged Russian and Eastern European connections within Turning Point USA, pointing to attendees at Charlie Kirk’s memorial event and several people linked to the organization. Blake Neff rejected those claims, arguing that Owens was connecting unrelated details without evidence. The allegations remain unverified, and the disagreement has added another public clash between the two conservative commentators.

stories.title: Supreme Court asks CBSE for details of steps taken to curb digital evaluation flubs
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has asked CBSE to detail its actions on digital evaluation issues. A one-member commission is now inquiring into these alleged irregularities. The court noted the frustration caused to students by these system problems. The Centre had previously removed CBSE officials and ordered an inquiry. Urgent action is needed to address students' concerns comprehensively.

stories.title: SIR exercise: Delhi voters get 10 more days to submit enumeration forms
stories.summary: Electors in Delhi now have an extended period to submit their enumeration forms. House-to-house visits by BLOs in Delhi will continue until August 8. Revised schedules have also been released for Punjab, Telangana, and Karnataka. The final electoral roll for Delhi will now be published on October 19. Similar extensions were previously announced for Andhra Pradesh and Haryana.

stories.title: Kudankulam nuclear plant data breached, NPCIL says core systems untouched
stories.summary: Nuclear Power Corporation of India stated its core systems remain secure after a cyber incident. A ransomware group posted files related to the Kudankulam nuclear plant online. Reliance Group confirmed a partial data breach on a third-party provider's server. These leaked files are not connected to nuclear safety or security systems. The incident involved conventional balance of plant common service facilities.

stories.title: Delhi high court judge, later Manipur CJ, had LPG agency during tenure
stories.summary: Justice Siddharth Mridul allegedly operated an LPG distributorship during his judicial service. This action appears to violate judicial ethics and conduct codes. Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited issued notices regarding the alleged contract violations. The agency dealership was eventually suspended by the oil company. The controversy involves a former judge and an oil marketing PSU.

stories.title: US launches fifth straight day of strikes on Iran, targets military sites near Hormuz
stories.summary: United States forces conducted new airstrikes against Iran on Wednesday. These strikes targeted coastal defense systems and missile infrastructure near the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian media reported explosions across southern Iran following the US attacks. Iran's parliament speaker described the conflict as an existential war with America. The renewed strikes further weakened hopes of reviving a recent ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: French prosecutors seek prison sentences and social media bans for streamers in Jean Pormanove case
stories.summary: French prosecutors seek jail time and platform bans for two streamers. They are accused of violent and humiliating online broadcasts involving Jean Pormanove. The content allegedly showed repeated mistreatment and was not simple entertainment. The streamers claim the videos were staged and agreed upon for viewers. A verdict in this case is expected on August 5.

stories.title: UK: Man charged with murder after Indian woman stabbed to death at home in London
stories.summary: A 24-year-old Indian woman was fatally stabbed at her London home. A man has been charged with murder and attempted murder in connection with the incident. The victim's family alleges the attack was racially motivated and seeks government assistance. They had sold land to fund her education and future aspirations in the UK. British Sikh groups express concern over rising race-based attacks targeting vulnerable individuals.

stories.title: UK: Man charged with murder after Indian woman stabbed to death at home in London
stories.summary: A 24-year-old Indian woman was fatally stabbed at her London home. A man has been charged with murder and attempted murder in connection with the incident. The victim's family alleges the attack was racially motivated and seeks government assistance. They had sold land to fund her education and future aspirations in the UK. British Sikh groups express concern over rising race-based attacks targeting vulnerable individuals.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir: In mourning, CM Omar Adhullah says Delhi protest is on
stories.summary: J&K CM Omar Abdullah confirmed the July 20 Delhi protest for statehood restoration. His party will travel to Delhi on July 19 to decide the next steps. National Conference invited 52 political figures for the planned federalism cause protest. Congress supports statehood plus, demanding land and job rights for the people. PDP has not yet clarified its stance on the National Conference invitation.

stories.title: Hurriyat Conference chairman Mirwaiz urges restraint as PoK unrest leaves 9 dead
stories.summary: Mirwaiz Umar Farooq urged Pakistan to defuse unrest in PoK through dialogue. He expressed anguish over civilian and police deaths in continuing unrest. Violence centers on a dispute over reserved seats for Kashmiri refugees in the assembly. Protesters want these seats scrapped, which Pakistan-based parties use for influence. Elections are scheduled for July 27, with a court ruling upholding the seats.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir: Pika gun ammo seized from hideout in Poonch; combing operation continues in neighbouring Rajouri
stories.summary: Security forces recovered 215 rounds of Pika gun ammunition from a terrorist hideout in Poonch. A search operation in Rajouri continued for a second day to trace two terror suspects. These suspects were captured on CCTV cameras crossing a road late Sunday. Joint operations are ongoing in forested areas of Rajouri and Poonch districts. These extensive combing operations aim to track down elusive militant groups.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Augustus: 'We write our names in the sand and then the waves roll in and...'
stories.summary: A thought-provoking quote from Neil Gaiman's comic series suggests that names written in sand reflect life's transient beauty, although it is incorrectly credited to Emperor Augustus Caesar. This notion echoes ancient philosophical themes of mortality and the futility of permanence. In contrast to the perceived eternal nature of digital existence, recognizing impermanence can free us from the burden of seeking to leave an indelible mark.

stories.title: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez voices concern over Clavicular’s influence on young men and Israel trip
stories.summary: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez voiced concerns about the looksmaxxing trend's influence. She worries about young men seeking acceptance through physical appearance changes. Ocasio-Cortez advocates for self-worth over solely focusing on physical looks. She also commented on streamer Clavicular's recent visit to Israel. The interview sparked social media debate on body positivity and online influence.

stories.title: Departement of space moves to stem exodus from key Isro missions; at least 100 quit in past few months: Sources
stories.summary: Isro's Department of Space has introduced new rules for scientist resignations. These new regulations aim to prevent departures from key projects like Gaganyaan. The department now requires central directors to refer all such requests to DoS. This move reverses a 2020 decision that empowered centre directors to accept resignations. Isro acknowledges departures but states it is prepared to manage the situation.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Cyrus the Great: 'All men have their frailties; and whoever looks for a friend...'
stories.summary: Cyrus the Great, an ancient king, cautioned against the pursuit of flawless friendships. He recognized that accepting human imperfections contributed to the foundation of a strong empire. In today's world, technology magnifies our quest for perfect relationships, often resulting in loneliness. This unrealistic pursuit stifles meaningful connections. By embracing imperfections, we can nurture deeper and more resilient bonds with one another.

stories.title: Amit Shah, Nitin Nabin among BJP top brass meet at PM Modi's residence
stories.summary: Top BJP leaders met at Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence on Wednesday. This meeting occurred just before the Parliament's upcoming session begins next week. The gathering included Home Minister Amit Shah and party president Nitin Nabin. Speculation is rife about potential reshuffles in the national office bearers team and Union cabinet. An NDA constituents meeting is also likely on July 21 to discuss floor strategy.

stories.title: This billionaire lived six months a year on his 233-foot superyacht to avoid paying land taxes
stories.summary: Innovative Microsoft engineer Charles Simonyi cleverly leveraged a bespoke superyacht to sidestep local taxation and stringent construction regulations. This mobile abode enabled him to traverse the globe while circumventing substantial property tax liabilities. His forward-thinking strategy predates ongoing discussions surrounding wealth taxation in high-levy regions. A trailblazer in digital technology and space tourism, he eventually acquired an even grander superyacht to enhance his aquatic adventures.

stories.title: Right to die: French Parliament approves assisted dying bill after years of debate
Red Fort to remain closed to public from July 15 to Aug 15
4-month-old undergoes rare lung-sparing surgery, recovers in just two days
Jones Act waiver extension on the table as Iran tensions threaten US fuel prices - report
Who is Kenichi Takano? Japanese man sentenced to 16 years for killing streamer Airi Sato during Tokyo livestream
stories.summary: Kenichi Takano has been sentenced to 16 years in prison for killing 22-year-old streamer Airi Sato during her livestream in Tokyo. The court found that he intentionally carried out the attack despite a financial dispute between them. The case shocked people around the world because thousands of viewers were watching Sato’s livestream when the attack happened, bringing renewed attention to creator safety.

stories.title: Cabinet approves Rs 25,000 cr Ganga, Varuna corridors for Varanasi
A scientist slipped into a pool beneath a US military base and found a 'demon cavefish'
stories.summary: In a remarkable finding, a scientist has uncovered a new species of eyeless fish in Bobcat Cave, aptly named the demon cavefish after a character from a popular TV series. This fascinating creature has evolved to thrive in complete darkness, displaying no eyes or pigmentation. Intriguingly, it cohabits with another sightless predator, showcasing the resilience of unique wildlife beneath humanity's constructed environments.

stories.title: 5,000 solar panels on an Alpine peak are producing three times more electricity thanks to snow reflection and colder temperatures
'Constructed without plan approval': 38 buildings at Azam Khan's Jauhar University to be demolished
stories.summary: The Rampur Development Authority ordered the demolition of thirty-eight university buildings. These structures were reportedly built without approved building plans by the authority. The university argued it was outside jurisdiction, but this was rejected by officials. Only two buildings had valid approvals, while others lacked necessary authorization. The constructions violated planning laws and are now liable for demolition.

stories.title: Isha Gramotsavam expands to North India, set to cover 10 states in biggest edition yet
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat to address women at Vishwa Mangalya Sabha meetings in Delhi, Hyderabad
Greenland lost 105 billion tonnes of ice as darkening surface speeds melting
'No dharna, lathi, placards, swords': Lok Sabha secretariat cautions MPs ahead of Monsoon session
10 largest lake islands in the world: From Manitoulin Island to Idjwi
stories.summary: Manitoulin Island in Canada is the world's largest freshwater lake island. René-Levasseur Island in Quebec was formed by a meteorite impact long ago. Sääminginsalo in Finland became an island after canal construction centuries ago. Olkhon Island in Russia's Lake Baikal features varied landscapes and cultural significance. These islands showcase diverse origins and remarkable freshwater environments globally.

stories.title: US woman arrested for sexually assaulting 2-year-old; identified by 'boobs' tattoo
Britain left a five-acre farm without crops; 15 years later, nature had turned it into...
stories.summary: An abandoned Norfolk farm field transformed into a vibrant wildflower meadow over a decade, as researchers monitored its evolution post-farming. Within ten to fifteen years, the area demonstrated an impressive resurgence of various plant species, emphasizing that simple, natural restoration techniques may outperform costly commercial methods. This evidence underscores the value of patience in reviving ecosystems and restoring lost habitats effectively.

stories.title: Indian truck driver Jashanpreet Singh jailed for nearly 5 years for deadly California crash

'Promise Me, America': Joe Biden to release new memoir on November 17 after US midterm polls
stories.summary: Joe Biden will release his new memoir, 'Promise Me, America,' on November 17. The book reflects on his presidency and his decisions regarding re-election. It will cover major events like the pandemic and international conflicts. The memoir's release follows the upcoming US midterm elections. Biden also mentioned his ongoing cancer treatment and recovery progress.

stories.title: Lion's mane jellyfish are washing up on New England beaches, and experts warn people not to touch them even after they die
Scientists found that white streetlights can trap more than 5,000 pill bugs in giant circular “death spirals,” exposing them to predators and wasting their energy
stories.summary: Researchers discovered land isopods forming massive, synchronized circular formations. These creatures, known as woodlice, were drawn into glowing traps by streetlights. The isopods marched in tight circles until exhaustion or predation stopped them. This behavior, observed in Israel's Golan Heights, poses risks to the small animals. Artificial light at night can inadvertently alter natural survival strategies.

stories.title: 'Jam-packed' with cockroaches: Kunal Kamra, Chandrashekhar Azad join CJP protest on day 25
Censor Board clearance for OTT films? Govt might amend IT Rules 2021 after row over 'Satluj'
stories.summary: The government is considering mandatory Central Board of Film Certification for OTT releases. This move would require amendments to existing IT rules for digital media. A recent controversy over the film Satluj on Zee5 prompted this consideration. Action may also be initiated against Zee5 for its release while under review. State governments are responsible for enforcing laws against private screenings of uncertified films.

stories.title: The Dutch police trained eagles to catch illegal drones, but the unusual experiment was later abandoned
Bali’s 1,000-year-old rice fields once worked as a giant water system. Now 6,500 hectares have vanished and locals are buying water
stories.summary: Bali's historic subak irrigation system is under pressure from tourism expansion. Thousands of hectares of rice fields have disappeared, impacting water availability. Increased demand from tourism facilities strains groundwater resources significantly. This loss threatens the subak system and ecological balance on the island. Preserving these terraces is crucial for water security and cultural heritage.

stories.title: Singapore turned wastewater into drinking water: How Singapore has treated the sewage water into liquid gold through NEWater, achieving a sustainable supply that exceeds World Health Organisation standards
'If Ramchandra married once, Rahim too should marry once': MP CM Mohan Yadav's UCC pitch
stories.summary: Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav strongly supports implementing a Uniform Civil Code. The state government plans to introduce a UCC Bill during the upcoming monsoon session. A committee submitted its report recommending UCC implementation, excluding tribal communities. The chief minister criticized the Congress party for its stance on the UCC issue. The government will also abide by the Supreme Court's decision on the Bhojshala dispute.
